lines.diplomatic: INCIPE Mænalios mecum mea tibia uersus;
lines.en: Begin with me, my pipe, the Maenalian verses;

loci.virgil: Incipe Maenalios mecum, mea tibia, versus.

lines.diplomatic: Pergite Pierides, GALLI dicamus amores.
lines.en: Proceed, Pierides [Muses], let us tell the loves of Gallus.

loci.virgil: Pergite, Pierides! Chromis et Mnasyllos in antro
incipe; sollicitos Galli dicamus amores,

lines.diplomatic: O decus ò famæ merito pars maxima nostræ,
lines.en: O glory, O deservedly the greatest part of our fame,

loci.virgil: O decus, o famae merito pars maxima nostrae,

lines.diplomatic: Te precor Alcide, cœptis ingentibus adsis,
lines.en: You I beseech, Alcides [Hercules], be present for these mighty undertakings,

loci.virgil: te precor, Alcide, coeptis ingentibus adsis.

lines.diplomatic: Dijs genite, & geniture Deos, assuesce uocari
lines.en: Begotten of gods, and destined to beget gods, grow accustomed to being invoked,

loci.virgil: dis genite et geniture deos. Iure omnia Bella
ingredere et votis iam nunc adsuesce vocari.

lines.diplomatic: Nulla meis sine te quæretur gloria rebus
lines.en: No glory shall be sought in my affairs without you;

loci.virgil: Nulla meis sine te quaeretur gloria rebus;

lines.diplomatic: Da facilem cursum, nihil hic nisi carmina desunt
lines.en: Grant an easy course; here nothing but songs is lacking.

loci.virgil: da facilem cursum atque audacibus adnue coeptis
experiar sensus nihil hic nisi carmina desunt.

lines.diplomatic: Rumpe moras: tentanda uia est, qua me quoq́; possim
lines.en: Break off delays: a way must be tried, by which I too might be able

loci.virgil: rumpe moras; vocat ingenti clamore Cithaeron
acer equis? Temptanda via est, qua me quoque possim

lines.diplomatic: Tollere humo ; stimulos sub pectore uertit Apollo
lines.en: to raise myself from the ground; Apollo turns the goads beneath my breast.

loci.virgil: concutit, et stimulos sub pectore vertit Apollo.

lines.diplomatic: Nymphæ, noster amor, præsentia numina, Fauni,
lines.en: Nymphs, our delight, present deities, Fauns,

loci.virgil: Nymphae, noster amor, Libethrides, aut mihi carmen,
et vos, agrestum praesentia numina, Fauni,

lines.diplomatic: Ore fauete omnes, & cingite baccare frontem
lines.en: Keep reverent silence, all of you, and bind my brow with baccar [cyclamen],

loci.virgil: Ore favete omnes, et cingite tempora ramis."
aut si ultra placitum laudarit, baccare frontem

lines.diplomatic: Cingite ne uati noceat mala lingua futuro.
lines.en: bind your brow, lest an evil tongue harm the poet to come.

lines.diplomatic: Hinc canere incipiam. Cum GALLVS amore periret
lines.en: From here I shall begin to sing. When Gallus was perishing of love,

loci.virgil: hinc canere incipiam. Vos, o clarissima mundi
Naides, indigno cum Gallus amore peribat?

lines.diplomatic: Quæ nemora, aut qui uos saltus habuere puellæ?
lines.en: what groves, or what glades held you, girls [Naiads]?

loci.virgil: Quae nemora, aut qui vos saltus habuere, puellae

lines.diplomatic: Pan deus Arcadiæ uenit, quem uidimus ipsi,
lines.en: Pan, the god of Arcadia, came, whom we ourselves saw,

loci.virgil: Pan deus Arcadiae venit, quem vidimus ipsi

lines.diplomatic: Venit & upilio: tardi uenere subulci,
lines.en: the shepherd came too; the slow swineherds came,

loci.virgil: venit et upilio; tardi venere subulci;

lines.diplomatic: Gens'q; uirum truncis, & duro robore nata
lines.en: and a race of men born of tree-trunks and hard oak,

loci.virgil: gensque virum truncis et duro robore nata,

lines.diplomatic: Nescia'q; humanis precibus mansuescere corda
lines.en: and hearts that do not know how to soften at human prayers.

loci.virgil: nesciaque humanis precibus mansuescere corda.

lines.diplomatic: Stant & oues circum, & crebris mugitibus amnes,
lines.en: The sheep stand around, and with frequent lowings the rivers

loci.virgil: Stant et oves circum;—nostri nec poenitet illas,
Balatu pecorum et crebris mugitibus amnes

lines.diplomatic: Arentes'q; sonant ripæ. Sub rupe iacentem
lines.en: and dry banks resound. Lying beneath a crag,

loci.virgil: Pinifer illum etiam sola sub rupe iacentem

lines.diplomatic: Heu miserande puer, cuncti se scire fatentur,
lines.en: alas, pitiable boy, all profess that they know;

loci.virgil: Heu, miserande puer, si qua fata aspera rumpas,
consulis, O bone rex: cuncti se scire fatentur,

lines.diplomatic: Te liquidi fleuere lacus, stragem'q; dedere
lines.en: the clear lakes wept for you, and the rivers wrought devastation,

loci.virgil: te liquidi flevere lacus.

lines.diplomatic: Flumina correptos unda torquentia montes:
lines.en: twisting in their current the mountains they had swept up:

lines.diplomatic: Qualis populea mœrens philomela sub umbra
lines.en: just as the nightingale, mourning beneath the poplar's shade,

loci.virgil: qualis populea maerens philomela sub umbra

lines.diplomatic: Atque Deos,atque astra uocat crudelia mater
lines.en: and the mother calls both the gods and the stars cruel,

loci.virgil: atque deos atque astra vocat crudelia mater.

lines.diplomatic: Mantua diues auis pectus percussa decorum
lines.en: Mantua, rich in forefathers, having struck her comely breast,

loci.virgil: Mantua, dives avis; sed non genus omnibus unum:
terque quaterque manu pectus percussa decorum,

lines.diplomatic: Ora puer prima signans intonsa iuuenta
lines.en: a boy, marking his unshorn face with the first [signs of] youth,

loci.virgil: ora puer prima signans intonsa iuventa.

lines.diplomatic: Cui pellis latos humeros,caput oris hiatus
lines.en: whose broad shoulders a hide, and whose head the gaping mouth

loci.virgil: cui pellis latos umeros erepta iuvenco
pugnatori operit, caput ingens oris hiatus

lines.diplomatic: Et malæ texere LVPI,cum dentibus albis
lines.en: and the jaws of a wolf covered him, with their white teeth,

lines.diplomatic: (Ille etiam & genti nomen dedit,arma´q; fixit)
lines.en: (he too gave his name to the race, and fixed [dedicated] arms)

loci.virgil: Teucrorum, et genti nomen dedit, armaque fixit

lines.diplomatic: Multa mouens animo syluas, saltus´q; peragrat
lines.en: pondering much in his mind, he ranges through woods and glades,

loci.virgil: multa movens animo iam tandem erumpit et inter
nescius; illa fuga silvas saltusque peragrat

lines.diplomatic: Noctes,atq; dies,est mollis flamma medullas.
lines.en: night and day, the soft flame devours his marrow.

loci.virgil: noctes atque dies patet atri ianua Ditis;
quid delubra iuvant? Est mollis flamma medullas

lines.diplomatic: Forté die,tardis ingens ubi flexibus errat
lines.en: By chance, one day, where huge, with slow windings, it wanders,

loci.virgil: Forte die sollemnem illo rex Arcas honorem
propter aquam. Tardis ingens ubi flexibus errat

lines.diplomatic: Mincius, auratus taurino cornua uultu,
lines.en: the Mincius, his horns gilded upon a bull-like face,

loci.virgil: et gemina auratus taurino cornua vultu

lines.diplomatic: Populeas inter frondes, lucos´q; sonantes
lines.en: among the poplar leaves, and the resounding groves,

loci.virgil: populeas inter frondes umbramque sororum
iam mihi per rupes videor lucosque sonantis

lines.diplomatic: Dum canit,& mœstum Musa solatur amorem:
lines.en: while he sings, and the Muse consoles his sorrowful love:

loci.virgil: dum canit et maestum Musa solatur amorem,

lines.diplomatic: Longe illi media se se tulit obuia sylua
lines.en: far off, in the middle of the wood, she came to meet him,

loci.virgil: longe illi dea mater erit, quae nube fugacem
Cui mater media sese tulit obvia silva,

lines.diplomatic: Causa mali tanti pulcherrima Deiopea,
lines.en: the cause of so great an evil, most beautiful Deiopea,

loci.virgil: Causa mali tanti coniunx iterum hospita Teucris
quarum quae forma pulcherrima Deiopea,

lines.diplomatic: Cui pharetra ex humero sonat arcus,& arma Dianæ,
lines.en: whose quiver sounds from her shoulder—the bow and arms of Diana—

loci.virgil: Cui pharetra ex auro, crines nodantur in aurum,
cuncta gerens, vocemque et corpus et arma Metisci.

lines.diplomatic: Qualis gemma micat,crines nodantur in aurum
lines.en: just as a gem gleams, her hair is bound up in gold,

loci.virgil: qualis gemma micat, fulvum quae dividit aurum,
Cui pharetra ex auro, crines nodantur in aurum,

lines.diplomatic: Aurea purpuream subnectit fibula uestem.
lines.en: a golden brooch fastens her purple gown.

lines.diplomatic: Agnouit iuuenis diuini signa decoris
lines.en: The youth recognized the marks of divine beauty;

loci.virgil: Adgnovit iuvenis duplicisque ad sidera palmas
est Dorycli coniunx; divini signa decoris

lines.diplomatic: Illi membra nouus soluit formidine torpor
lines.en: a strange numbness loosened his limbs with fear;

loci.virgil: Olli membra novus solvit formidine torpor,

lines.diplomatic: Obstupuit primo aspectu,& uox faucibus hæsit
lines.en: he was struck dumb at the first sight, and his voice stuck in his throat;

loci.virgil: Obstipuit primo aspectu Sidonia Dido,
Obstipui, steteruntque comae et vox faucibus haesit.

lines.diplomatic: Vt primum fari potuit, sic incipit ore
lines.en: as soon as he could speak, thus he began:

loci.virgil: Ut primum fari potuit, sic institit ore:

lines.diplomatic: Suspirans, imo´q; trahens à pectore uocem,
lines.en: sighing, and drawing his voice from the depths of his breast:

loci.virgil: suspirans, imoque trahens a pectore vocem:

lines.diplomatic: Cara deùm soboles animo gratissima nostro
lines.en: "Dear offspring of the gods, most welcome to my heart,

loci.virgil: cara deum suboles, magnum Iovis incrementum!
"Nympha, decus fluviorum, animo gratissima nostro,

lines.diplomatic: Salue uera Iouis proles,mea maxima cura,
lines.en: hail, true offspring of Jove, my greatest care,

loci.virgil: Salve, vera Iovis proles, decus addite divis,
Sidoniam puer ire parat, mea maxima cura,

lines.diplomatic: Quam nec longa dies pietas nec mitigat ulla,
lines.en: whom neither length of days nor any devotion softens,

loci.virgil: quam nec longa dies, pietas nec mitigat ulla,

lines.diplomatic: Sola ne perpetua mærens carpere iuuenta,
lines.en: will you alone waste away, grieving, in perpetual youth,

loci.virgil: solane perpetua maerens carpere iuventa,

lines.diplomatic: Iam matura uiro? Veneris nec premia noris?
lines.en: already ripe for a husband? And will you never know the rewards of Venus?

loci.virgil: iam matura viro, iam plenis nubilis annis.
nec dulcis natos, Veneris nec praemia noris?

lines.diplomatic: Ah uirgo infelix,mitte hanc de pectore curam.
lines.en: Ah, unhappy maiden, cast this care from your breast;

loci.virgil: ah, virgo infelix, quae te dementia cepit!
Dardanidae venient; mitte hanc de pectore curam;

lines.diplomatic: Vtere sorte tua,nimium ne crede colori
lines.en: make use of your lot, and do not trust too much in your beauty;

loci.virgil: "utere sorte tua. Miseri te siqua parentis
o formose puer, nimium ne crede colori!

lines.diplomatic: Omnia fert ætas,fugit irreparabile tempus.
lines.en: age carries off all things, irretrievable time flees."

loci.virgil: Omnia fert aetas, animum quoque: saepe ego longos
Sed fugit interea, fugit inreparabile tempus,

lines.diplomatic: Alma præcor miserere animi non digna ferentis,
lines.en: "Kindly one, I beg, have mercy on a spirit bearing things it does not deserve,

loci.virgil: alma, precor, miserere;---potes namque omnia, nec te
tantorum, miserere animi non digna ferentis."

lines.diplomatic: Ad te confugio, & supplex tua numina posco.
lines.en: to you I flee for refuge, and as a suppliant I beg your divine favor."

loci.virgil: ad te confugio et supplex tua numina posco.

lines.diplomatic: Vix ea fatus erat, ueluti uiolauerit ostro
lines.en: Scarcely had he spoken these words: just as if someone had stained

loci.virgil: Vix ea fatus erat, cum circumfusa repente
Indum sanguineo veluti violaverit ostro

lines.diplomatic: Si quis ebur, tales uirgo dabat ore colores :
lines.en: ivory with purple, such colors the maiden showed upon her face:

loci.virgil: alba rosa: talis virgo dabat ore colores.

lines.diplomatic: Deiecit uultum, & demissa uoce locuta est.
lines.en: she cast down her gaze, and spoke with lowered voice:

loci.virgil: Deiecit vultum et demissa voce locuta est:

lines.diplomatic: Desine meq́; tuis incendere, teq́, querelis,
lines.en: "Cease to inflame both me and yourself with your complaints;

loci.virgil: Desine meque tuis incendere teque querelis:

lines.diplomatic: Quam pro me curam geris, hanc precor, optime, pro me
lines.en: the care which you bear for my sake, this, I beg, best one, for my sake

loci.virgil: "Quam pro me curam geris, hanc precor, optime, pro me

lines.diplomatic: Deponas, toties iam dedignata maritos
lines.en: set aside — I who have so often already disdained suitors;

loci.virgil: quos ego sim totiens iam dedignata maritos?

lines.diplomatic: Mens immota manet sola contenta Diana
lines.en: my mind remains unmoved, content with Diana alone;

loci.virgil: mens immota manet; lacrimae volvuntur inanes.
optavere nurum: sola contenta Diana

lines.diplomatic: Nanque fatebor enim, non uitæ gaudia quæro.
lines.en: for — I will confess it — I do not seek the joys of life;

loci.virgil: namque, fatebor enim, dum me Galatea tenebat,
fortunaeque locus. Non vitae gaudia quaero,

lines.diplomatic: Certum est in syluis, inter deserta ferarum
lines.en: it is resolved, in the woods, amid the wild beasts' deserted haunts,

loci.virgil: certum est in silvis, inter spelaea ferarum
Talem inter silvas, inter deserta ferarum,

lines.diplomatic: Malle pati incœptum frustra submitte furorem.
lines.en: I am resolved to prefer to endure. Lay aside the frenzy you have begun in vain.

loci.virgil: malle pati, tenerisque meos incidere amores
Verum age et inceptum frustra submitte furorem

lines.diplomatic: Disce puer uirtutem ex me, & non temnere diuos
lines.en: "Learn, boy, virtue from me, and not to scorn the gods;

loci.virgil: "Disce, puer, virtutem ex me verumque laborem,
"Discite iustitiam moniti, et non temnere divos."

lines.diplomatic: Hic pietatis honos. Patet atri ianua Ditis.
lines.en: This is the reward of piety. The gate of black Dis stands open;

loci.virgil: Hic pietatis honos? Sic nos in sceptra reponis?"
noctes atque dies patet atri ianua Ditis;

lines.diplomatic: Quæsitor Minos uitasq́;, & crimina discit,
lines.en: Minos, the inquisitor, examines lives and crimes,

loci.virgil: quaesitor Minos urnam movet; ille silentum

lines.diplomatic: Castigatq;, auditq́; dolos : te triste manebit
lines.en: and chastises, and hears out deceits: a grim [reckoning] awaits you,

loci.virgil: O miseri. Te, Turne, nefas, te triste manebit

lines.diplomatic: Supplicium, uotisq́; deos uenerabere seris.
lines.en: a punishment, and too late, with prayers, you will worship the gods."

lines.diplomatic: Sic ait, & dictis diuinum aspirat amorem,
lines.en: So she speaks, and with her words breathes divine love [into him],

loci.virgil: Sic ait: illa gradum studio celerabat anili.
incipit et dictis divinum adspirat amorem:

lines.diplomatic: Edocet humanis quæ sit fiducia rebus -
lines.en: she teaches him what trust may be placed in human affairs —

loci.virgil: edocet, humanis quae sit fiducia rebus

lines.diplomatic: Illum turbat Amor magis, ægrescitq́; medendo.
lines.en: Love disturbs him all the more, and he sickens from the very curing of it.

loci.virgil: Illum turbat amor, figitque in virgine voltus:
flectitur: exsuperat magis aegrescitque medendo.

lines.diplomatic: Tum quassans caput hæc effudit pectore dicta.
lines.en: Then, shaking his head, he poured out these words from his breast:

loci.virgil: Tum quassans caput haec effundit pectore dicta:

lines.diplomatic: Omnia percepi, atque animo mecum ante peregi
lines.en: "I have understood everything, and already gone through it beforehand in my mind;

loci.virgil: omnia praecepi atque animo mecum ante peregi.

lines.diplomatic: Ne tantos mihi finge metus: non talia curat;
lines.en: do not fashion such great fears for me: such things are no concern of his;

loci.virgil: Ne tantos mihi finge metus; nec regia Iuno
“Ecquis erit modus?” inquit; “Amor non talia curat;

lines.diplomatic: Omnia uincit Amor, strepitumq́; Acherontis auari
lines.en: Love conquers all, and the roar of greedy Acheron

loci.virgil: omnia vincit Amor; et nos cedamus Amori.”
subiecit pedibus strepitumque Acherontis avari.

lines.diplomatic: Subiecit pedibus: Quis enim modus adsit Amori ?
lines.en: he has cast beneath his feet: for what measure could there be to Love?

loci.virgil: me tamen urit amor; quis enim modus adsit amori?

lines.diplomatic: Inde hominum pecudumq; genus, pictæq́, uolucres
lines.en: Thence the race of men and of cattle, and the painted birds,

loci.virgil: Inde hominum pecudumque genus, vitaeque volantum,
et genus aequoreum, pecudes pictaeque volucres,

lines.diplomatic: Et genus æquoreum genitalia semina poscunt,
lines.en: and the race of the sea, seek the seeds of generation,

loci.virgil: et genus aequoreum, pecudes pictaeque volucres,
vere tument terrae et genitalia semina poscunt.

lines.diplomatic: In furias, ignemq́; ruunt. Regina sacerdos
lines.en: they rush into frenzy and fire. The priestess-queen,

loci.virgil: in furias. ignemque ruunt. Amor omnibus idem.
gente sub Hectorea, donec regina sacerdos,

lines.diplomatic: Marte grauis, partu sub luminis edidit oras
lines.en: heavy with Mars [pregnant by him], brought forth in travail into the light

loci.virgil: furtivum partu sub luminis edidit oras,

lines.diplomatic: Romanos rerum dominos gentemq́; togatam.
lines.en: the Romans, lords of the world and the toga-clad race.

loci.virgil: Romanos rerum dominos gentemque togatam:

lines.diplomatic: Quid maiora sequar ? pueri, innuptæq́; puellæ
lines.en: Why should I pursue greater things? Boys, and unwed girls

loci.virgil: quid maiora sequar?—salices humilesque genestae
magnanimum heroum, pueri innuptaeque puellae,

lines.diplomatic: Magnanimi Iouis ingratum ascendére cubile
lines.en: ascended the unwelcome couch of great-hearted Jove.

loci.virgil: magnanimi Iovis ingratum ascendere cubile,

lines.diplomatic: Et dubitant homines NATVRÆ accedere parteis?
lines.en: And do men hesitate to take up Nature's tasks?

loci.virgil: Et dubitant homines serere atque inpendere curam
Sin, has ne possim naturae accedere partis,

lines.diplomatic: Nymphæ laurentes, præstanti corpore Nymphæ
lines.en: Laurentine nymphs, nymphs of surpassing bodily beauty,

loci.virgil: Ipse inter primos praestanti corpore Turnus
"Nymphae, Laurentes nymphae, genus amnibus unde est,

lines.diplomatic: Degere more feræ, quæ uos dementia adegit ?
lines.en: to live after the manner of a wild beast — what madness has driven you [to this]?

loci.virgil: degere, more ferae, tales nec tangere curas!
Quis deus Italiam, quae vos dementia adegit

lines.diplomatic: Vana superstitio in dumis coluisse Dianam,
lines.en: vain superstition, to have worshipped Diana amid the thickets,

loci.virgil: vana superstitio veterumque ignara deorum
Nec tibi desertae in dumis coluisse Dianam

lines.diplomatic: AEternum telorum, & uirginitatis amorem :
lines.en: an eternal love of weapons and of virginity:

loci.virgil: aeternum telorum et virginitatis amorem

lines.diplomatic: Egregiam uero laudem, & spolia ampla refertis,
lines.en: splendid praise indeed, and ample spoils you bring back —

loci.virgil: "Egregiam vero laudem et spolia ampla refertis

lines.diplomatic: Tantorum impensis operum nihil omnibus actum.
lines.en: after the cost of such great efforts, for all that nothing has been accomplished.

loci.virgil: tantorum impensis operum, nil dona neque aurum

lines.diplomatic: Tu ne tot incassum fusos patiere labores?
lines.en: Will you suffer so many labors to have been spent in vain?

loci.virgil: "Turne, tot incassum fusos patiere labores

lines.diplomatic: Quin potius miserere: mori me denique coges .
lines.en: Rather take pity: you will finally force me to die.

loci.virgil: Quin potius pacem aeternam pactosque hymenaeos
Nil nostri miserere? Mori me denique coges.

lines.diplomatic: Accipe, daq; fidem. quoniam conuenimus ambo,
lines.en: Receive my pledge, and give yours in turn; since we two have come together,

loci.virgil: Accipe daque fidem: sunt nobis fortia bello
Cur non, Mopse, boni quoniam convenimus ambo,

lines.diplomatic: Vis ěgo inter nos, quid possit uterq; uicissim
lines.en: Do you wish, then, that between us what each of us in turn can do

loci.virgil: Vis ergo inter nos quid possit uterque vicissim

lines.diplomatic: Experiamur?
lines.en: let us try?

lines.diplomatic: Nec sum adeo informis. solum te uirgine dignum,
lines.en: Nor am I so ill-formed. You alone [I hold] worthy of the maiden,

loci.virgil: Nec sum adeo informis: nuper me in litore vidi,
Euhoe Bacche, fremens, solum te virgine dignum

lines.diplomatic: Et me Phœbus amat; nouit nanq; omnia uates,
lines.en: and Phoebus loves me too; for the seer knows all things,

loci.virgil: Et me Phoebus amat; Phoebo sua semper apud me
grandaevus Nereus; novit namque omnia vates,

lines.diplomatic: Te nemus omne canet; si quid mea carmina possunt
lines.en: the whole grove shall sing of you; if my songs can do anything,

loci.virgil: te nemus omne canet; nec Phoebo gratior ulla est,
Fortunati ambo! Siquid mea carmina possunt,

lines.diplomatic: Semper honos, nomenq; tuum laudesq; manebunt,
lines.en: your honor, and your name, and your praises shall ever remain,

loci.virgil: semper honos nomenque tuum laudesque manebunt,

lines.diplomatic: Si te nulla mouet tantarum gloria rerum,
lines.en: if no glory of such great things moves you,

loci.virgil: Si te nulla movet tantarum gloria rerum,

lines.diplomatic: Huc geminas nunc flecte acies, res aspice nostras.
lines.en: turn now both your eyes hither, look upon our affairs.

loci.virgil: "Huc geminas nunc flecte acies, hanc aspice gentem
parce pio generi, et propius res aspice nostras.

lines.diplomatic: Pandite nunc Helicona Deæ, cantusq; mouete.
lines.en: Open now Helicon, goddesses, and set your songs in motion.

loci.virgil: Pandite nunc Helicona, deae, cantusque movete,

lines.en: but the immortal race, having followed the precepts of God,

lines.en: they choose laws and magistrates, and a sacred senate,

loci.virgil: aut aris servare sacros aut scindere terram

lines.en: not if I had a hundred tongues, and a hundred mouths,

loci.virgil: Non, mihi si linguae centum sint oraque centum,

lines.en: rush toward the worse, and, slipping back, are carried backward.

lines.en: then let him know [it]: if anyone [would behold] the airy Alps and the Norican,

loci.virgil: Tum sciat, aerias Alpis et Norica si quis

lines.en: let him see the strongholds on the hills, and the deserted kingdoms,

loci.virgil: nunc quoque post tanto videat desertaque regna

lines.en: having embraced all the heaven-dwellers, a hundred grandsons,

Iunoni infernae dictus sacer; hunc tegit omnis

loci.virgil: Hinc Italae gentes omnisque Oenotria tellus

loci.virgil: at secura quies et nescia fallere vita,

lines.diplomatic: Cura tibi Diuùm effigies, & templa tueri:

loci.virgil: Cura tibi divom effigies et templa tueri:

flumina, nec somnos abrumpit cura salubris.

lines.en: and would that I had been one of you, and one of your own,

loci.virgil: Atque utinam ex vobis unus, vestrique fuissem

lines.en: either a guardian of the flock, or a vintner of the ripe grape:

me tamen urit amor; quis enim modus adsit amori?

loci.virgil: regibus incessit magno discordia motu,

lines.en: and the Morini, farthest of mankind; so many thousand peoples --

adventante dea. "Procul O procul este, profani,"

lines.en: sent forth into empire -- he to whom the stars of heaven are obedient,

loci.virgil: missus in imperium magnum. Cui deinde subibit,
cui pecudum fibrae, caeli cui sidera parent

lines.diplomatic: Inferniq; latus, atque altæ mœnia Romæ
lines.en: and the flank of the underworld, and the walls of lofty Rome.

loci.virgil: Albanique patres, atque altae moenia Romae.

lines.diplomatic: Sed fugit interea fugit irreparabile tempus.
lines.en: But meanwhile time flies, flies beyond recall.

loci.virgil: Sed fugit interea, fugit inreparabile tempus,

lines.diplomatic: Accipite ergo animis atque hæc mea figite dicta
lines.en: Receive, therefore, into your minds, and fix fast these my words:

loci.virgil: "Accipite ergo animis atque haec mea figite dicta.

lines.diplomatic: Rectores iuuenum, lætasq; aduertite mentes
lines.en: ye guides of youth, turn hither your joyful minds,

loci.virgil: rectores iuvenum et rerum dedit esse magistros.
"Accipite haec animis, laetasque advertite mentes:

lines.diplomatic: Et nati natorum, & qui nascentur ab illis.
lines.en: and the sons of sons, and those who shall be born from them.

loci.virgil: et nati natorum, et qui nascentur ab illis."

lines.diplomatic: Monstrū horrendū ingens, uariū et mutabile sẽper
lines.en: A monster huge and dreadful, ever fickle and changeable --

loci.virgil: monstrum horrendum, ingens, cui, quot sunt corpore plumae
Heia age, rumpe moras. Varium et mutabile semper

lines.diplomatic: FOEMINA, quæ uentis uolucriq; simillima somno
lines.en: WOMAN, who is most like the winds, and most like a winged dream,

loci.virgil: par levibus ventis volucrique simillima somno.

lines.diplomatic: Mobilitate uiget, linguis micat ore trisulcis
lines.en: thrives by her fickleness, [and] flickers with three-forked tongues from her mouth,

loci.virgil: mobilitate viget, viresque adquirit eundo,
arduus ad solem et linguis micat ore trisulcis.

lines.diplomatic: Tam ficti prauiq́; tenax quam nuntia ueri
lines.en: as tenacious of the false and the depraved as she is a messenger of the true.

loci.virgil: tam ficti pravique tenax, quam nuntia veri.

lines.diplomatic: Dat sine mente sonum, totoq́; ardentis ab ore
lines.en: she gives forth sound without sense, and from her whole burning face

loci.virgil: dat sine mente sonum gressusque effingit euntis,
His agitur furiis; totoque ardentis ab ore

lines.diplomatic: Scintillæ absistunt, oculis micat acribus ignis
lines.en: sparks fly off, [and] fire flashes from her keen eyes.

lines.diplomatic: Sola domo mœret uacua, cui carmina semper
lines.en: alone she grieves in the empty house -- she to whom songs are ever [dear]

loci.virgil: sola domo maeret vacua, stratisque relictis
Crethea Musarum comitem, cui carmina semper

lines.diplomatic: Et citharæ cordi, pernicibus ignea plantis
lines.en: and the lyre are dear to her heart; fiery, with swift feet,

loci.virgil: haec fatur virgo et pernicibus ignea plantis

lines.diplomatic: Omnia peruolitat latè loca, pectore uersat
lines.en: she flits through all places far and wide, turns over in her breast

loci.virgil: omnia pervolitat late loca iamque sub auras
At Cytherea novas artes, nova pectore versat

lines.diplomatic: Mille nocendi artes quis fallere possit amantem
lines.en: a thousand arts of doing harm -- who could deceive a lover [like her]?

loci.virgil: mille nocendi artes. Fecundum concute pectus,
At regina dolos---quis fallere possit amantem?

lines.diplomatic: Omnibus in templis, gaudens popularibus auris
lines.en: in all the temples, rejoicing in the favoring breath of the crowd,

loci.virgil: omnibus in templis matrum chorus, omnibus arae;
nunc quoque iam nimium gaudens popularibus auris.

lines.diplomatic: Fert picturatas auri sub tegmine uestes
lines.en: she wears figured, embroidered robes, beneath a covering of gold,

loci.virgil: fert picturatas auri subtemine vestes

lines.diplomatic: Aurea subnectens exertæ cingula mammæ
lines.en: fastening golden girdles beneath her bared breast,

loci.virgil: aurea subnectens exsertae cingula mammae,

lines.diplomatic: Et gradiens ima uerrit uestigia cauda
lines.en: and as she walks she sweeps her tracks with the end of her trailing tail,

loci.virgil: et gradiens ima verrit vestigia cauda,

lines.diplomatic: Purpureoq́; altæ suras euincta cothurno
lines.en: and, her calves bound high in a purple buskin,

loci.virgil: purpureoque alte suras vincire cothurno.
puniceo stabis suras evincta coturno.

lines.diplomatic: Sanguineis frontem moris & tempora pingit
lines.en: she paints her brow and temples with blood-red mulberries,

loci.virgil: sanguineis frontem moris et tempora pingit.

lines.diplomatic: Mille trahit uarios aduerso sole colores
lines.en: she draws a thousand varied colors, facing the sun,

loci.virgil: mille iacit varios adverso sole colores.

lines.diplomatic: Flagrantes perfusa genas, it pectore summo
lines.en: her burning cheeks suffused [with color]; across the top of her breast there runs [the circlet],

loci.virgil: flagrantis perfusa genas, quoi plurimus ignem
pars levis umero pharetras; it pectore summo

lines.diplomatic: Flexilis obtorti per collum circulus auri,
lines.en: a pliant circlet of twisted gold about her neck,

lines.diplomatic: Tecti auro fuluum crines nodantur in aurum.
lines.en: covered with gold, her locks are knotted up into tawny gold.

loci.virgil: tecti auro fulvum mandunt sub dentibus aurum;
Cui pharetra ex auro, crines nodantur in aurum,

lines.diplomatic: Ambrosiæq́; comæ diuinum uertice odorem
lines.en: and [her] ambrosial locks, from the crown of her head, a divine fragrance

loci.virgil: ambrosiaeque comae divinum vertice odorem

lines.diplomatic: Spirauere, humeros oleo perfusa nitescit
lines.en: breathed forth; her shoulders, drenched with oil, gleam.

loci.virgil: nudatosque umeros oleo perfilsa nitescit.

lines.diplomatic: Qualis gemma micat, circum caput egit honestum
lines.en: as a gem gleams; she turned her comely head about,

loci.virgil: qualis gemma micat, fulvum quae dividit aurum,
et quocumque deus circum caput egit honestum.

lines.diplomatic: Ardentes dare uisa faces, mirabile uisu,
lines.en: she seemed to give off burning torches -- a wonder to behold --

loci.virgil: ardentes dare visa faces: "Hic quaerite Troiam;
convertunt clamore fugam, mirabile visu,

lines.diplomatic: Aera dimouit tenebrosum, & dispulit umbras
lines.en: she parted the murky air, and scattered the shadows,

loci.virgil: ara dimovit tenebrosum et dispulit umbras,

lines.diplomatic: Hinc atque hinc, tantum egregio decus enitet ore
lines.en: on this side and on that; so great a splendor shines from her surpassing face,

loci.virgil: Hinc atque hinc vastae rupes geminique minantur
Aeneas; tantum egregio decus enitet ore.

lines.diplomatic: Præpetibus pennis magnas it fama per urbes :
lines.en: on swift wings Rumour goes through great cities:

loci.virgil: praepetibus pennis ausus se credere caelo,
Extemplo Libyae magnas it Fama per urbes---

lines.diplomatic: Hæc passim dea fœda uirùm diffundit in ora
lines.en: these things the foul goddess spreads everywhere into the mouths of men.

loci.virgil: Haec passim dea foeda virum diffundit in ora.
Haec passim dea foeda virum diffundit in ora.

lines.diplomatic: Illam omnis tectis agrisq́; effusa iuuentus
lines.en: toward her all the youth, poured forth from houses and fields,

loci.virgil: Illam omnis tectis agrisque effusa iuventus

lines.diplomatic: Circunfusa ruit, pesti deuota futuræ
lines.en: rushes, crowding round about -- [youth] devoted to a doom to come --

loci.virgil: circumfusa ruit, certantque inludere capto.
Praecipue infelix, pesti devota futurae,

lines.diplomatic: Attonitis inhians animis prospectat euntem
lines.en: gaping, with minds astonished, it gazes upon her as she passes,

loci.virgil: attonitis inhians animis, ut regius ostro
turbaque miratur matrum et prospectat euntem,

lines.diplomatic: Nec uidisse semel satis est, iuuat usque morari
lines.en: nor is it enough to have seen [her] once; it delights them to linger on,

loci.virgil: nec vidisse semel satis est; iuvat usque morari,

lines.diplomatic: Sensit læta, suæ contra non immęmor artis
lines.en: she perceived it, glad, and, for her part, not unmindful of her own art,

loci.virgil: Sensit laeta dolis et formae conscia coniunx.
occupat. Ille suae contra non immemor artis

lines.diplomatic: Pestis & ira Deum, flammantia lumina torquens
lines.en: a plague and the wrath of the gods, rolling flaming eyes,

loci.virgil: pestis et ira deum Stygiis sese extulit undis.
exsilit in siccum et flammantia lumina torquens

lines.diplomatic: Tum laqueis captare feras, & fallere uisco
lines.en: then to catch wild beasts with snares, and deceive [birds] with birdlime,

loci.virgil: tum laqueis captare feras et fallere visco

lines.diplomatic: Cum spes arrectæ iuuenum, & furialia membra
lines.en: when the hopes of the youths are raised, and [she takes on] fury-driven limbs,

loci.virgil: cum spes arrectae iuvenum, exsultantiaque haurit
Allecto torvam faciem et furialia membra

lines.diplomatic: Dulcibus illa,quidem illecebris mortalibus ægris
lines.en: she indeed, with sweet enticements, [works] upon wretched mortals,

loci.virgil: dulcibus illa quidem inlecebris, et saepe superbos
adparent acuuntque metum mortalibus aegris,

lines.diplomatic: Nequid inexpertum , cithara fidibusq; canoris
lines.en: so that nothing be left untried -- with the lyre and tuneful strings,

loci.virgil: Threcia fretus cithara fidibusque canoris,

lines.diplomatic: Pertentat sensus, rapuit´q; in fomite flammam
lines.en: she thoroughly assails the senses, and has caught flame in the tinder,

loci.virgil: pertemptat sensus atque ossibus implicat ignem
nutrimenta dedit, rapuitque in fomite flammam.

lines.diplomatic: At iuuenis magnum cui uersat in ossibus ignem
lines.en: but the youth, in whose bones a great fire is stirred by

loci.virgil: At iuvenis, vicisse dolo ratus, avolat ipse,
Quid iuvenis, magnum cui versat in ossibus ignem

lines.diplomatic: Durus amor, neque enim membris dat cura quietem,
lines.en: harsh love; for indeed care grants no rest to his limbs,

loci.virgil: Aeneas (neque enim membris dat cura quietem)

lines.diplomatic: Stare loco nescit. subita spe feruidus ardet
lines.en: he cannot stand still in one place. He burns, feverish with sudden hope,

loci.virgil: stare loco nescit, micat auribus et tremit artus
turbatosque duces, subita spe fervidus ardet:

lines.diplomatic: Attollit´q; animos horrendum´q; intonat armis
lines.en: and he lifts up his spirit, and thunders dreadfully with his arms,

loci.virgil: attollitque animos. Poenorum qualis in arvis
laetitia exsultans, horrendumque intonat armis;

lines.diplomatic: Quadrupedem´q; citum ferrato calce fatigat
lines.en: and he wearies his swift steed with iron-shod heel,

lines.diplomatic: Cuius olorinæ surgunt de uertice pennæ
lines.en: from whose crest rise swan's feathers,

loci.virgil: cuius olorinae surgunt de vertice pennae,

lines.diplomatic: Pictus acu clamydem, & ferrugine clarus hibera
lines.en: his cloak embroidered with the needle, and bright with Iberian rust-red,

loci.virgil: pictus acu chlamydem et ferrugine clarus Hibera,

lines.diplomatic: Tela manu iaciens uolucres diuerberat auras
lines.en: hurling missiles with his hand, he cleaves the flying breezes,

loci.virgil: tela manu iaciens, ter secum Trous heros
Hyrtacidae iuvenis volucres diverberat auras;

lines.diplomatic: Ostentans artem , figit´q; in uirgine uultus
lines.en: displaying [his] skill, and fixes his gaze upon the maiden,

loci.virgil: Illum turbat amor, figitque in virgine voltus:

lines.diplomatic: Is´q; amens animi ,clypeum´q; auroq; trilicem
lines.en: and he, frantic in spirit, [puts on] his shield and, triple-woven with gold,

loci.virgil: Isque amens animi et rumore accensus amaro
ad iuga cogit equos clipeumque auroque trilicem

lines.diplomatic: Loricam induitur, ualidam ui corripit hastam
lines.en: puts on his breastplate, [and] with force seizes a strong spear,

loci.virgil: aedibus adstabat, validam vi corripit hastam,

lines.diplomatic: Vrbe furens, pugnæ´q; ciet simulachra sub armis
lines.en: raging through the city, and stirs up mock battles under arms,

loci.virgil: urbe furens, qualis coniecta cerva sagitta,
impediunt, pugnaeque cient simulacra sub armis;

lines.diplomatic: It cælo.clamor´q; uirum clangor´q; tubarum
lines.en: it rises to heaven -- the shout of men and the blare of trumpets.

loci.virgil: it caelo clamorque virum clangorque tubarum.

lines.diplomatic: Posthinc digressus pingues spatiatur ad aras
lines.en: then, having gone off from here, he paces to the rich altars.

loci.virgil: aut ante ora deum pinguis spatiatur ad aras,

lines.diplomatic: Et nunc huc,inde huc,incertos explicat orbes
lines.en: And now this way, now that, he traces uncertain circles,

loci.virgil: et nunc huc, inde huc incertos implicat orbes

lines.diplomatic: Ceu quondam torto uolitans sub uerbere turbo
lines.en: as once, whirling, a top under the twisted lash,

loci.virgil: Ceu quondam torto volitans sub verbere turbo,

lines.diplomatic: Interdum genua impediunt, cursum´q; recusant
lines.en: at times [his] knees fail [him], and he refuses the course;

loci.virgil: interdum genua impediunt cursumque recusant,

lines.diplomatic: Languescit moriens, obsedit limen amatæ
lines.en: he grows faint, dying; he has besieged the threshold of [his] beloved.

loci.virgil: languescit moriens lassove papavera collo
celsa petit tacitumque obsedit limen Amatae,

lines.diplomatic: Primitiæ iuuenis miseræ, terræ´q; per umbram
lines.en: The wretched first-fruits of the youth, and through the shadow of the earth,

loci.virgil: Primitiae iuvenis miserae bellique propinqui
Nocte volat caeli medio terraeque per umbram,

lines.diplomatic: Stridens, nec dulci declinat lumina somno
lines.en: shrieking, nor does he close his eyes in sweet sleep.

lines.diplomatic: Quid faceret?solans ægrum testudine amorem
lines.en: What was he to do? soothing his sick love with the lyre,

loci.virgil: Quid faceret? Quo se rapta bis coniuge ferret?
Ipse cava solans aegrum testudine amorem

lines.diplomatic: Talia uoce refert,gemitum dat pestore ab imo .
lines.en: such things he utters with his voice, he gives a groan from the depths of his breast.

loci.virgil: talia voce refert: "O terque quaterque beati,
Tum vero ingentem gemitum dat pectore ab imo,

lines.diplomatic: O decus Italiæ uirgo, mea maxima cura
lines.en: O glory of Italy, maiden, my greatest care,

loci.virgil: "O decus Italiae virgo, quas dicere grates
Sidoniam puer ire parat, mea maxima cura,

lines.diplomatic: Nil nostri miserere,mori me denique cogis
lines.en: you have no pity on me, you drive me at last to die;

loci.virgil: Nil nostri miserere? Mori me denique coges.

lines.diplomatic: Victus amore tui uentos perpessus, & imbreis
lines.en: conquered by love of you, having endured winds and rains,

loci.virgil: Victus amore tui, cognato sanguine victus
cum fremit ad caulas, ventos perpessus et imbris,

lines.diplomatic: Nocte super media supplex ad limina ueni
lines.en: at dead of night I came, a suppliant, to [your] threshold.

loci.virgil: obieci caput et supplex ad limina veni.

lines.diplomatic: Per te, per qui te talem genuere parentes
lines.en: By you, by the parents who begot you such as you are,

loci.virgil: "Per te, per qui te talem genuere parentes,

lines.diplomatic: Da dextram misero, noctem non amplius unam
lines.en: give your right hand to a wretched man; not one night more

loci.virgil: da dextram misero, et tecum me tolle per undas,
Tu faciem illius noctem non amplius unam

lines.diplomatic: Extremam hanc oro ueniam, miserere laborum
lines.en: this last favor I beg, have pity on [my] toils,

loci.virgil: Extremam hanc oro veniam---miserere sororis---
intemerata fides, oro, miserere laborum

lines.diplomatic: Alma precor miserere animi non digna ferentis
lines.en: kindly one, I pray, have pity, on a mind bearing what it does not deserve.

loci.virgil: alma, precor, miserere;---potes namque omnia, nec te
tantorum, miserere animi non digna ferentis."

lines.diplomatic: Nec sum adeo informis, nympharum sanguinis una
lines.en: Nor am I so ill-favored, O one of the blood of nymphs.

loci.virgil: Nec sum adeo informis: nuper me in litore vidi,
an Phoebi soror? an nympharum sanguinis una?---

lines.diplomatic: O quoties, & quæ nobis Galatea locuta est
lines.en: O how often, and what things has Galatea said to us!

loci.virgil: O quotiens et quae nobis Galatea locuta est!

lines.diplomatic: Vritur infelix, nam me discedere fleuit
lines.en: Unhappy, she burns; for she wept at my leaving.

loci.virgil: Uritur infelix Dido, totaque vagatur
Phyllida amo ante alias; nam me discedere flevit,

lines.diplomatic: Fors & uota facit tua dum uestigia lustro
lines.en: Perhaps she also makes vows, while I trace your footsteps,

loci.virgil: fors et vota facit cumulatque altaria donis:
at mecum raucis, tua dum vestigia lustro,

lines.diplomatic: Et me Phœbus amat, si quid mea carmina possunt
lines.en: and Phoebus loves me, if my songs can do anything;

loci.virgil: Et me Phoebus amat; Phoebo sua semper apud me
Fortunati ambo! Siquid mea carmina possunt,

lines.diplomatic: Semper honos nomenq; tuum laudesq; manebunt
lines.en: always your honor and name and praises will remain.

loci.virgil: semper honos nomenque tuum laudesque manebunt;

lines.diplomatic: Tu modo promissis maneas sub nocte silenti
lines.en: Only remain true to [your] promises, beneath the silent night;

loci.virgil: Tu modo promissis maneas, servataque serves
rura tenent, somno positae sub nocte silenti

lines.diplomatic: Vtere sorte tua, multos ignaua per annos
lines.en: make use of your lot, [you who have been] idle through so many years,

loci.virgil: "utere sorte tua. Miseri te siqua parentis
et nemora evertit multos ignava per annos

lines.diplomatic: Causando nostros in longum ducis amores
lines.en: by making excuses you draw out our love at length,

loci.virgil: Causando nostros in longum ducis amores:

lines.diplomatic: Nec mea iam mutata loco sententia cedit
lines.en: nor does my resolve, now shifted from its place, yield.

loci.virgil: nec mea iam mutata loco sententia cedit:

lines.diplomatic: Quem fugis ah demens, en hæc promissa fides est?
lines.en: Whom do you flee, ah madwoman? is this the faith [you] promised?

loci.virgil: Quem fugis, ah, demens? Habitarunt di quoque silvas,
venturum Ausonios. En haec promissa fides est?"

lines.diplomatic: Siste gradum; quis te nostris complexibus arcet?
lines.en: Stay your step; who keeps you from our embraces?

loci.virgil: Siste gradum, teque aspectu ne subtrahe nostro.
"Quem fugis, aut quis te nostris complexibus arcet?"

lines.diplomatic: O digno coniuncta uiro sors omnia uersat
lines.en: O you joined to a worthy husband, fortune overturns all things;

loci.virgil: O digno coniuncta viro, dum despicis omnes,
nunc victi, tristes, quoniam Fors omnia versat,

lines.diplomatic: Nusquam tuta fides, crudelem abrumpere uitam
lines.en: nowhere is faith safe; to break off [this] cruel life

loci.virgil: Nusquam tuta fides. Eiectum litore, egentem
nunc O nunc liceat crudelem abrumpere vitam,

lines.diplomatic: Mens imota manet, à quæ iam satis ima dehiscat.
lines.en: my mind remains unmoved; ah, what [earth] might now gape deep enough,

loci.virgil: Italiam regeret, genus alto a sanguine Teucri
accipio! Quid ago? Aut quae iam satis ima dehiscat

lines.diplomatic: Terra mihi, uos ò potius miserescite uenti,
lines.en: for me — but you, O winds, rather take pity,

loci.virgil: vana feror. Quod ut O potius formidine falsa

lines.diplomatic: Et nostras audite preces, sæuiq; doloris
lines.en: and hear our prayers, and of [my] fierce grief

loci.virgil: et nostras audite preces. Si tangere portus
necdum etiam causae irarum saevique dolores

lines.diplomatic: Partem aliquam uenti diuum referatis ad aures
lines.en: carry some part back, O winds, to the ears of the gods;

loci.virgil: partem aliquam, venti, divom referatis ad auris!

lines.diplomatic: Exoriare aliquis nostris ex ossibus ultor
lines.en: arise, some avenger, from my bones!

loci.virgil: Exoriare aliquis nostris ex ossibus ultor,

lines.diplomatic: Hæc precor, hanc uocem extremam cum sanguine fundo
lines.en: This I pray, this last utterance I pour forth with [my] blood.

loci.virgil: Haec precor, hanc vocem extremam cum sanguine fundo.

lines.diplomatic: Agnouit longe gemitum formosa iuuenca
lines.en: The lovely heifer [i.e. the girl] recognized the groan from afar,

loci.virgil: Agnovit longe gemitum praesaga mali mens:
Pascitur in magna Sila formosa iuvenca:

lines.diplomatic: Virginis os habitumq; gerens, risuq; soluto
lines.en: wearing a maiden's face and garb, and with laughter unrestrained,

loci.virgil: virginis os habitumque gerens, et virginis arma
versibus incomptis ludunt risuque soluto

lines.diplomatic: Ardua tecta petit, stabuli & de culmine summo
lines.en: she makes for the lofty roofs, and from the highest peak of the stable

loci.virgil: ardua tecta petit stabuli et de culmine summo

lines.diplomatic: Nam quis te iuuenum confidentissime nostras
lines.en: — for who, most presumptuous of youths, bade you

loci.virgil: “Nam quis te, iuvenum confidentissime, nostras

lines.diplomatic: Iussit adire domos? de te nil tale uerebar
lines.en: approach our home? I feared no such thing of you —

loci.virgil: Nisus ad haec: "Equidem de te nil tale verebar

lines.diplomatic: Desine meq; tuis incendere teq; querelis
lines.en: cease to inflame both me and yourself with your complaints.

loci.virgil: Desine meque tuis incendere teque querelis:

lines.diplomatic: Hác iter est, quà te ducit uia dirige gressum
lines.en: This is the way; where the road leads you, direct your step.

loci.virgil: Hac iter est. Tu, ne qua manus se attollere nobis
Perge modo, et, qua te ducit via, dirige gressum."

lines.diplomatic: Hæc effata silet, uana spe lusit amantem
lines.en: Having said this she falls silent; she mocked the lover with vain hope.

loci.virgil: Haec effata silet; pallor simul occupat ora.
multa malus simulans, vana spe lusit amantem.

lines.diplomatic: Sepsit se tectis coniunx ubi pristinus illi
lines.en: She shut herself within [her] house, where her former husband, to her,

loci.virgil: saepsit se tectis rerumque reliquit habenas.
in nemus umbriferum, coniunx ubi pristinus illi

lines.diplomatic: Lætitia exultans,neruoq; obuersus equino
lines.en: exulting with joy, and turned [toward her] with his horse's sinew,

loci.virgil: laetitia exsultans, horrendumque intonat armis;
non tulit Ascanius nervoque obversus equino

lines.diplomatic: Optatos dedit amplexus, curasq; resoluit
lines.en: gave [her] the longed-for embraces, and loosed [her] cares.

loci.virgil: optatos dedit amplexus placidumque petivit
Invitat genialis hiems curasque resolvit,

lines.diplomatic: Diues opum diues pictai uestis, & auri
lines.en: Rich in wealth, rich in embroidered robe and gold;

loci.virgil: dives inaccessos ubi Solis filia lucos
dives equum, dives picta vestis et auri;

lines.diplomatic: Hic focus, & tædæ pingues firmissima uina,
lines.en: here [is] the hearth, and the fat pine-torches, the strongest wines,

loci.virgil: Hic focus et taedae pingues, hic plurimus ignis
Sunt et Amineae vites, firmissima vina,

lines.diplomatic: Castaneæ molles, epulæq; ante ora paratæ
lines.en: soft chestnuts, and feasts set out before [their] eyes,

loci.virgil: impositique rogis iuvenes ante ora parentum:

lines.diplomatic: Regifico luxu, biforem dat tibia cantum
lines.en: with kingly luxury; the flute gives forth its twofold strain,

loci.virgil: Dindyma ubi adsuetis biforem dat tibia cantum!

lines.diplomatic: Instauratq; choros, ille asper & improbus ira
lines.en: and renews the dances; he, harsh and reckless in his wrath,

loci.virgil: instauratque choros, mixtique altaria circum
balatum exercent, ille asper et improbus ira

lines.diplomatic: Ac ueluti pleno lupus insidiatus ouili
lines.en: and just as a wolf lying in wait at a full sheepfold

loci.virgil: Ac veluti pleno lupus insidiatus ovili

lines.diplomatic: Sæuit in absenteis, & cælum territat armis
lines.en: rages against the absent [flock], and terrifies the sky with [clashing] arms;

loci.virgil: saevit in absentis, collecta fatigat edendi
castra fugae fidens et caelum territat armis.

lines.diplomatic: Ense leuis nudo, parmaq; inglorius alba
lines.en: light with [his] bare sword, and inglorious with [his] blank shield,

loci.virgil: ense levis nudo parmaque inglorius alba;

lines.diplomatic: Tum pudor incendit uires & conscia uirtus
lines.en: then shame and courage conscious [of itself] kindle [his] strength;

loci.virgil: Tum pudor incendit vires et conscia virtus,

lines.diplomatic: Arietat in portas & duros obice postes,
lines.en: he batters at the gates, and the posts made hard with a bar,

loci.virgil: arietat in portas et duros obice postis.

lines.diplomatic: Infelix uates spe multum captus inani
lines.en: the unhappy poet, much taken by empty hope,

loci.virgil: infelix vates, rumpitque hanc pectore vocem:
Et nunc ille quidem spe multum captus inani

lines.diplomatic: Multa gemens ignominiam, uestigia retro
lines.en: groaning much over [his] disgrace, [he turns his] steps back,

loci.virgil: multa gemens ignominiam plagasque superbi
fallacis silvae?" Simul et vestigia retro

lines.diplomatic: Improperata refert,magno inflammatus amore
lines.en: retraces them unhurried, inflamed with great love;

loci.virgil: improperata refert, et mens exaestuat ira.
Ast illum, ereptae magno inflammatus amore

lines.diplomatic: Respicit ignarus rerum, ingratusq; salutis
lines.en: he looks back, ignorant of [what has happened], and ungrateful for [his] safety.

loci.virgil: Respicit ignarus rerum ingratusque salutis

lines.diplomatic: Interea toto non secius aere ningit
lines.en: Meanwhile it snows just the same through the whole sky;

loci.virgil: Interea toto non setius aere ninguit:

lines.diplomatic: Illi alternantes linguis uibrantibus ora
lines.en: they, taking turns, with quivering tongues [each other's] mouths

loci.virgil: illi alternantes multa vi proelia miscent
sibila lambebant linguis vibrantibus ora.

lines.diplomatic: Ore legunt, tacitum pertentant gaudia pectus
lines.en: they gather with [their] mouths; joys thrill through [their] silent breast,

loci.virgil: ore legunt, ipsae regem parvosque Quirites
Latonae tacitum pertemptant gaudia pectus:

lines.diplomatic: Complexi inter se noctemq; diemq; morantur
lines.en: embracing each other they linger through night and day.

loci.virgil: complexi inter se noctemque diemque morantur.

lines.diplomatic: Heu miserande puer quæ te dementia cepit ?
lines.en: Alas, pitiable boy, what madness has seized you?

loci.virgil: Heu, miserande puer, si qua fata aspera rumpas,
Ah, Corydon, Corydon, quae te dementia cepit!

lines.diplomatic: Quo moriture ruis aliena ad pabula fucus ?
lines.en: Where are you rushing, doomed to die, [like] a drone to another's fodder?

loci.virgil: "Quo moriture ruis maioraque viribus audes?
immunisque sedens aliena ad pabula fucus

lines.diplomatic: Fallit te incautum tantarum gloria rerum
lines.en: The glory of such great things deceives you, unwary [as you are];

loci.virgil: Fallit te incautum pietas tua." Nec minus ille
Si nulla accendit tantarum gloria rerum,

lines.diplomatic: O formose puer nimium ne crede colori
lines.en: O beautiful boy, do not trust too much to [your] complexion.

loci.virgil: o formose puer, nimium ne crede colori!

lines.diplomatic: Nil ualidæ iuuere manus, lumenq; iuuentæ
lines.en: [His] strong hands availed nothing, nor the light of [his] youth,

loci.virgil: nec validae iuvere manus genitorque Melampus,
caesariem nato genetrix lumenque iuventae

lines.diplomatic: Purpureum, nihil illa deos, nil carmina curat
lines.en: purple/radiant [though it was]; she cares nothing for the gods, nothing for songs.

loci.virgil: adgrediar, nihil ille deos, nil carmina curat.

lines.diplomatic: Fatiferumq; ensem, loricam ex ære rigentem,
lines.en: and the fate-bringing sword, the breastplate stiff with bronze,

loci.virgil: fatiferumque ensem, loricam ex aere rigentem

lines.diplomatic: Instratos ostro alipedes,cristasq; comantes
lines.en: the swift-footed horses draped in purple, and the flowing crests,

loci.virgil: instratos ostro alipedes pictisque tapetis;

lines.diplomatic: Conuectare iuuat prædas, & uiuere rapto
lines.en: it delights [her] to gather plunder, and to live by pillage;

loci.virgil: comportare iuvat praedas et vivere rapto.

lines.diplomatic: Hic amor hoc studium patriæ, communis Erinnys
lines.en: this is [her] love, this [her] zeal — the common Fury of [her] country —

loci.virgil: hic amor, hoc studium, dum sacra secundus haruspex
praemetuens, Troiae et patriae communis Erinys,

lines.diplomatic: Vt gemma bibat, & sarrano dormiat ostro
lines.en: that she may drink from a jeweled [cup], and sleep in Tyrian purple;

loci.virgil: ut gemma bibat et Sarrano dormiat ostro;

lines.diplomatic: Visceribus miserorum & sanguine uescitur atro
lines.en: she feeds on the entrails of the wretched, and on black blood;

loci.virgil: Visceribus miserorum et sanguine vescitur atro.

lines.diplomatic: Suadet enim uesana fames, manditq; trabitq;
lines.en: for mad hunger urges [her] on, and she gnaws and drags

loci.virgil: (suadet enim vesana fames) manditque trahitque

lines.diplomatic: Molle pecus, mutumq́; metu, de more uetusto
lines.en: the soft flock, mute with fear, according to ancient custom,

loci.virgil: Arcades ad portas ruere et de more vetusto

lines.diplomatic: Munera portantes nunc hos nunc accipit illos
lines.en: [those] bringing gifts — now these, now those, she receives.

loci.virgil: munera portantis aurique eborisque talenta
Navita sed tristis nunc hos nunc accipit illos,

lines.diplomatic: Aedibus in medijs, coram data copia fandi
lines.en: In the midst of the halls, opportunity is granted to speak face to face;

loci.virgil: Aedibus in mediis nudoque sub aetheris axe
Postquam introgressi et coram data copia fandi,

lines.diplomatic: Tum demum admissi stagna exoptata reuisunt.
lines.en: then at last, admitted, they revisit the longed-for pools.

loci.virgil: tum demum admissi stagna exoptata revisunt."

lines.diplomatic: Ast alios longe summotos arcet arena
lines.en: But others, kept far off, the shore bars away;

loci.virgil: ast alios longe submotos arcet harena.

lines.diplomatic: Centum errant annos, lachrymæ uoluuntur inanes.
lines.en: for a hundred years they wander, [their] tears rolling in vain.

loci.virgil: Centum errant annos volitantque haec litora circum;
mens immota manet; lacrimae volvuntur inanes.

lines.diplomatic: Gorgones Harpyæ multa mercede domandæ
lines.en: Gorgons, Harpies, to be tamed at great cost,

loci.virgil: cogendae in sulcum ac multa mercede domandae.

lines.diplomatic: Ignauum fucos pecus à præsepibus arcent
lines.en: they drive the idle drones, [that worthless] herd, from the hives;

loci.virgil: ignavum fucos pecus a praesepibus arcent.

lines.diplomatic: Haud ignota loquor, magnam Mauortis ad urbem
lines.en: I speak of no unknown things: to the great city of Mars

loci.virgil: haud ignota loquor---superis concessit ab oris,
Quantos ille virum magnam Mavortis ad urbem

lines.diplomatic: Non unquam grauis ære domum mihi dextra redibat
lines.en: never did [my] hand come home heavy with bronze;

loci.virgil: non umquam gravis aere domum mihi dextra redibat.

lines.diplomatic: Munere sic niueo lanæ te Luna fefellit
lines.en: by this snow-white gift of wool, O Moon, did [he] deceive you,

loci.virgil: Munere sic niveo lanae, si credere dignum est,
Pan deus Arcadiae captam te, Luna, fefellit

lines.diplomatic: Pan ouium custos, nouit nanq; omnia uates,
lines.en: Pan, guardian of sheep — for the seer knows all things —

loci.virgil: Pan, ovium custos, tua si tibi Maenala curae,
grandaevus Nereus; novit namque omnia vates,

lines.diplomatic: In nemora alta uocans, nec tu aspernata uocantem
lines.en: calling [you] into the deep groves; nor did you scorn [him] calling.

loci.virgil: in nemora alta vocans; nec tu aspernata vocantem.

lines.diplomatic: Quid dominæ facient? carpentes pensa puellæ
lines.en: What will the mistresses do? — girls plying [their] wool-tasks —

loci.virgil: Quid domini faciant, audent cum talia fures!
Ne nocturna quidem carpentes pensa puellae

lines.diplomatic: Et petiere sibi monimentum & pignus amoris
lines.en: and they sought for themselves a memorial and pledge of love,

loci.virgil: et petiere sibi et voluere adiungere gentes;
ferre sui dederat monumentum et pignus amoris."

lines.diplomatic: Pallamq́; & pictum croceo uelamen acantho
lines.en: and a mantle, and a veil embroidered with saffron acanthus.

loci.virgil: [pallamque et pictum croceo velamen acantho.]

lines.diplomatic: His animaduersis atque hæc exempla secuti
lines.en: Having observed these things, and having followed these examples,

loci.virgil: his animadversis terram multo ante memento
His quidam signis atque haec exempla secuti

lines.diplomatic: O socij, quæ dicam animis aduertite uestris
lines.en: O comrades, turn your minds to what I shall say:

loci.virgil: "O socii---neque enim ignari sumus ante malorum---
vos, famuli, quae dicam, animis advertite vestris.

lines.diplomatic: Ingens argentum patribus dat iura uocatis
lines.en: vast [store of] silver gives laws to the fathers summoned,

loci.virgil: ingens argentum mensis, caelataque in auro
indicitque forum et patribus dat iura vocatis.

lines.diplomatic: Sceptra tenens; mollitq; animos, & temperat iras
lines.en: holding the scepter; and he softens [their] spirits, and tempers [their] wrath.

loci.virgil: sceptra tenens, mollitque animos et temperat iras.

lines.diplomatic: Frigoribus medijs animum inflammauit amore;
lines.en: In the midst of the frosts he inflamed [her] heart with love,

loci.virgil: nec si frigoribus mediis Hebrumque bibamus,
His dictis incensum animum inflammavit amore,

lines.diplomatic: Spemq́; dedit dubiæ menti, soluitq́; pudorem
lines.en: and gave hope to [her] wavering mind, and loosed [her] modesty;

loci.virgil: spemque dedit dubiae menti, solvitque pudorem.

lines.diplomatic: Limina perrumpit, postes'q, à cardine uellit
lines.en: he bursts through the threshold, and tears the doorposts from the hinge.

loci.virgil: limina perrumpit, postisque a cardine vellit

lines.diplomatic: Quare agite ò iuuenes, si fert ita corde uoluptas
lines.en: Wherefore come now, o youths, if pleasure so inclines in [your] heart

loci.virgil: Quare agite, o iuvenes, tantarum in munere laudum
incolimus. Sed vos, si fert ita corde voluntas,

lines.diplomatic: Rumpere claustra mànu STYGIAMq; innare paludem
lines.en: to burst the bars with [your] hand, and to swim the Stygian marsh

loci.virgil: rumpere claustra manu sociosque immittere portis,
flumina tanta paras Stygiamque innare paludem---

lines.diplomatic: Informi limo, manibus date LILIA plenis
lines.en: in the shapeless mire — give lilies with full hands

loci.virgil: informi limo glaucaque exponit in ulva.
tu Marcellus eris. Manibus date lilia plenis,

lines.diplomatic: Aurea, nunc ea uisa salus morientibus una
lines.en: Golden — now she was seen as the one salvation for the dying

loci.virgil: aurea nunc, olim silvestribus horrida dumis.
Lenaeos; ea visa salus morientibus una;

lines.diplomatic: Ante fores, subito stridentes cardine sacræ
lines.en: Before the doors, suddenly creaking on their hinge — the sacred [doors]

loci.virgil: ante fores subito non voltus, non color unus,
Tum demum horrisono stridentes cardine sacrae

lines.diplomatic: Panduntur portæ, & fauces graue olentis Auerni
lines.en: The gates are thrown open, and the jaws of heavy-reeking Avernus

loci.virgil: Inde ubi venere ad fauces grave olentis Averni,

lines.diplomatic: Sed fugite o miseri, fugite hinc, latet anguis in herba
lines.en: But flee, o wretched ones, flee hence — a snake lurks in the grass

loci.virgil: Sed fugite, O miseri, fugite, atque ab litore funem
frigidus, O pueri, fugite hinc, latet anguis in herba.

lines.diplomatic: vipeream inspirans animam, lasciua puella
lines.en: breathing [into you] a viperous spirit — the wanton girl

loci.virgil: vipeream inspirans animam: fit tortile collo
Malo me Galatea petit, lasciva puella,

lines.diplomatic: Cum dabit amplexus, atque oscula dulcia figet
lines.en: when she will give embraces, and will plant sweet kisses

loci.virgil: cum dabit amplexus atque oscula dulcia figet,

lines.diplomatic: Nuda genu, nodoq; sinus collecta fluentes
lines.en: bare at the knee, her flowing garment gathered with a knot

loci.virgil: nuda genu, nodoque sinus collecta fluentis.

lines.diplomatic: Vos agitate fugam direptis crura cothurnis
lines.en: You take to flight, your legs stripped of their buskins

loci.virgil: vos agitate fugam:
tingue novo mecum direptis crura cothurnis.

lines.diplomatic: Attrectare nefas, talis se se halitus atris
lines.en: to touch [it is] unlawful — such a breath from black [jaws]

loci.virgil: attrectare nefas, donec me flumine vivo
tendere iter pennis---talis sese halitus atris

lines.diplomatic: Faucibus effundens nares contingit odore
lines.en: pouring itself forth from [its] throat, strikes the nostrils with its smell

loci.virgil: obicit et noto naris contingit odore,

lines.diplomatic: Turbidus hic cœno uastaq; uoragine gurges
lines.en: Here a turbid whirlpool, with its vast abyss, [muddy] with mire

loci.virgil: Turbidus hic caeno vastaque voragine gurges

lines.diplomatic: Pestiferas aperit fauces, furor impius intus
lines.en: opens its plague-bearing jaws; impious Rage [dwells] within

loci.virgil: pestiferas aperit fauces, quis condita Erinys,
claudentur Belli portae; Furor impius intus,

lines.diplomatic: Pallentesq; habitant morbi sub rupe cauata
lines.en: and pale Diseases dwell beneath the hollowed rock

loci.virgil: pallentesque habitant Morbi, tristisque Senectus,
Classem in convexo nemorum sub rupe cavata

lines.diplomatic: Quo lati ducunt aditus, nemus imminet umbra
lines.en: where the wide approaches lead, a grove looms over with its shade

loci.virgil: quo lati ducunt aditus centum, ostia centum;
desuper horrentique atrum nemus imminet umbra.

lines.diplomatic: Desuper horrenti; folijsq; sub omnibus hærent
lines.en: bristling from above; and beneath every leaf they cling

loci.virgil: Pana tenere ferunt, foliisque sub omnibus haerent.

lines.diplomatic: Obscenæ uolucres, uariarum monstra ferarum
lines.en: Foul birds, monsters of every kind of wild beast

loci.virgil: obscenae volucres: alarum verbera nosco
Multaque praeterea variarum monstra ferarum:

lines.diplomatic: Nota nimis miseris, cernis custodia qualis
lines.en: too well known to the wretched — you see what sort of guard

loci.virgil: nota nimis miseris atroque fluentia tabo.
panduntur portae. Cernis custodia qualis

lines.diplomatic: O prestans animi iuuenis noctesq; diesq;
lines.en: O youth outstanding in courage — night and day

loci.virgil: "O praestans animi iuvenis, quantum ipse feroci
vestibulum exsomnis servat noctesque diesque,

lines.diplomatic: Vestibulo sedeat, primisq; in faucibus orci
lines.en: sits in the vestibule, and in the first jaws of Orcus

loci.virgil: vestibulo sedeat, facies quae limina servet?
Vestibulum ante ipsum, primisque in faucibus Orci

lines.diplomatic: Sæuior intus habet sedem durissima regna
lines.en: more savage within holds its seat — the harshest realm

loci.virgil: saevior intus habet sedem. Tum Tartarus ipse
Gnosius haec Rhadamanthus habet, durissima regna,

lines.diplomatic: Pallida Tisiphone flammisq; armata chimæra
lines.en: Pale Tisiphone, and the Chimaera armed with flames

loci.virgil: pallida Tisiphone Morbos agit ante Metumque,
horrendum stridens, flammisque armata Chimaera,

lines.diplomatic: Hic labor ille domus, & inextricabilis error
lines.en: Here [is] that labor of the house, and the inextricable maze

loci.virgil: hic labor ille domus et inextricabilis error;

lines.diplomatic: Heu fuge crudeles terras, fuge littus auarum
lines.en: Alas, flee the cruel lands, flee the greedy shore

loci.virgil: Heu, fuge crudelis terras, fuge litus avarum:

lines.diplomatic: Disce puer uirtutem ex me, & non temnere diuos
lines.en: Learn virtue from me, boy, and not to scorn the gods

loci.virgil: "Disce, puer, virtutem ex me verumque laborem,
"Discite iustitiam moniti, et non temnere divos."

lines.diplomatic: Nulli fas casto sceleratum insistere limen
lines.en: It is right for no chaste person to set foot on the accursed threshold

loci.virgil: nulli fas casto sceleratum insistere limen;

lines.diplomatic: Porta aduersa ingens exhalat opaca mephytim
lines.en: The huge gate facing [us], dark, breathes out a foul stench

loci.virgil: Porta adversa ingens, solidoque adamante columnae,
fonte sonat saevamque exhalat opaca mephitim.

lines.diplomatic: Vnde cauæ tepido sudant humore lacunæ
lines.en: whence the hollow pools sweat with warm moisture

loci.virgil: unde cavae tepido sudant humore lacunae.

lines.diplomatic: Hic quos durus Amor crudeli tabe peredit
lines.en: Here [are] those whom harsh Love has consumed with cruel wasting

loci.virgil: Hic, quos durus amor crudeli tabe peredit,

lines.diplomatic: Fluctibus oppressos rapidus uorat æquore uortex
lines.en: Overwhelmed by the waves, the swift whirlpool devours them in its flood

loci.virgil: fluctibus oppressos Troas caelique ruina,
torquet agens circum, et rapidus vorat aequore vortex.

lines.diplomatic: Prospectum eripiens oculis immane baratrum
lines.en: snatching the view from their eyes — a huge abyss

loci.virgil: prospectum eripiens oculis, glomeratque sub antro
pallida, dis invisa, superque immane barathrum

lines.diplomatic: Ignari scelerum, & primæuo flore iuuentus
lines.en: Unaware of crimes, and youth in its earliest flower

loci.virgil: ignari scelerum tantorum artisque Pelasgae.
Ante urbem pueri et primaevo flore iuventus

lines.diplomatic: Siue errore uiæ, seu tempestatibus acti
lines.en: whether driven by wandering of the way, or by storms

loci.virgil: Sive errore viae seu tempestatibus acti,

lines.diplomatic: In uada præcipitant. fundo uoluuntur in imo
lines.en: they plunge headlong into the shoals; they are rolled in the lowest depth

loci.virgil: in vada praecipitant, cum Iuppiter horridus austris
fulmine deiecti fundo volvuntur in imo.

lines.diplomatic: Limosoq; lacu pugnando uulnera passi
lines.en: and in the miry lake, having suffered wounds in fighting

loci.virgil: limosoque lacu per noctem obscurus in ulva
Hic manus ob patriam pugnando volnera passi,

lines.diplomatic: purpurei cristis, iuuenes auroq; corusci
lines.en: purple with crests, youths gleaming with gold

loci.virgil: purpurei cristis iuvenes auroque corusci.

lines.diplomatic: Inualidiq; senes, iuuenum tentare laborem
lines.en: and feeble old men, to attempt the labor of young men

loci.virgil: invalidique senes turris ac tecta domorum
ausus et ipse manu iuvenum temptare laborem.

lines.diplomatic: Ausi omnes, immane nefas, ausoq; potiti
lines.en: All dared it — a monstrous crime — and gained possession of what they dared

loci.virgil: ausi omnes immane nefas, ausoque potiti.

lines.diplomatic: Quid maiora sequar. genus insuperabile bello
lines.en: Why should I pursue greater things? A race unconquerable in war

loci.virgil: quid maiora sequar?—salices humilesque genestae
Hinc Gaetulae urbes, genus insuperabile bello,

lines.diplomatic: Magnanimum Heroum, lacerum crudeliter ora
lines.en: of great-souled heroes — [the race] cruelly mangled in the face —

loci.virgil: magnanimum heroum, pueri innuptaeque puellae,
Deiphobum videt et lacerum crudeliter ora,

lines.diplomatic: Ora manusq́; ambas, caligine uoluitur atra
lines.en: his face and both hands — he is whirled along in black gloom

loci.virgil: "Quis globus, o cives, caligine volvitur atra?

lines.diplomatic: Per pice torrenteis atraq; uoragine ripas
lines.en: through banks seething with pitch and black whirling abyss

loci.virgil: per pice torrentis atraque voragine ripas

lines.diplomatic: Quiq; sacerdotes casti dum uita manebat
lines.en: and those who were chaste priests while life remained

loci.virgil: quique sacerdotes casti, dum vita manebat,

lines.diplomatic: Quiq; pij uates nimirum hæc illa charybdis
lines.en: and those who [were] pious bards — truly this is that Charybdis

loci.virgil: Et pater Anchises: "Nimirum haec illa Charybdis:

lines.diplomatic: Hos Helenus scopulos, hæc saxa horrenda canebat
lines.en: of these crags Helenus, of these dreadful rocks, used to sing

lines.diplomatic: Dij prohibete minas, dij talem auertite casum
lines.en: Gods, forbid these threats; gods, avert such a fate

loci.virgil: "Di, prohibete minas; di, talem avertite casum,

lines.diplomatic: Vos animam hanc potius quocunque absumite læto
lines.en: Take this life of mine instead, by whatever death

loci.virgil: Vos animam hanc potius quocumque absumite leto."

lines.diplomatic: Si pereo manibus hominum perijsse iuuabit
lines.en: If I perish, it will be a comfort to have perished by the hands of men

loci.virgil: Si pereo, hominum manibus periisse iuvabit."

lines.diplomatic: O pater, an ne aliquas ad cælum hinc ire putandũ est?
lines.en: O father, must it be thought that any [souls] go hence to heaven?

loci.virgil: "O pater, anne aliquas ad caelum hinc ire putandum est

lines.diplomatic: Aspicis hæc? an te genitor cum fulmina torques
lines.en: Do you see these things? Or, father, when you hurl [your] thunderbolts,

loci.virgil: aspicis haec, an te, genitor, cum fulmina torques,

lines.diplomatic: Nequicquam horremus? nostri non plena laboris
lines.en: do we shudder in vain? [Is there any region] not full of our suffering,

loci.virgil: quae regio in terris nostri non plena laboris?

lines.diplomatic: Quæ regio in terris? nullo discrimine cædem
lines.en: what region on earth? With no distinction, savage slaughter

loci.virgil: quae regio in terris nostri non plena laboris?
terribilis saevam nullo discrimine caedem

lines.diplomatic: Suscitat, irarumq; omnes effundit habenas
lines.en: she stirs up, and lets loose all the reins of [her] wrath,

lines.diplomatic: More furens torrentis aquæ, uel turbinis atri
lines.en: raging like a torrent of water, or a black whirlwind,

loci.virgil: more furens. Tandem erumpunt et castra relinquunt
Dardanius, torrentis aquae vel turbinis atri

lines.diplomatic: Effera uis animi, subigit decernere amantes
lines.en: the savage force of [her] spirit drives lovers to contend with one another,

loci.virgil: effera vis animi? "Contra Tyrrhenus, ut auras
cornibus inter se subigit decernere amantis.

lines.diplomatic: Vulneribus crebris, dominorum fallere dextras
lines.en: with frequent wounds, [and drives them] to betray their masters' hands

loci.virgil: volneribus crebris, lavit ater corpora sanguis,
impia nec veriti dominorum fallere dextras,

lines.diplomatic: Infelix monstrum, quo non præstantius ullum
lines.en: unhappy monster, than which none [is] more outstanding,

loci.virgil: dat signum caelo, quo non praesentius ullum

lines.diplomatic: Ore uomens ignes, armare in prælia fratres
lines.en: vomiting fires from [its] mouth — [she] can arm brothers, of one mind, for battles,

loci.virgil: ore vomens ignis magna se mole ferebat.
Tu potes unanimos armare in proelia fratres

lines.diplomatic: Atque odijs uersare domos, ruit omnia late
lines.en: and overturn homes with hatreds; she lays all things low far and wide,

loci.virgil: arboribus stragemque satis, ruet omnia late;

lines.diplomatic: Fœmina, palantes utroque ab littore gentes
lines.en: Woman — the nations wandering scattered from either shore,

loci.virgil: Femina palantis agit atque haec agmina vertit!
bisque triumphatas utroque ab litore gentes.

lines.diplomatic: Territat inualidas ut aues populosq; feroces
lines.en: she terrifies, as [she terrifies] feeble birds, and fierce peoples,

loci.virgil: territat invalidas ut aves et litora vestra
per medias urbes agitur populosque feroces.

lines.diplomatic: Vestigat lustrans, pedibusq; euiscerat uncis
lines.en: she tracks, searching, and disembowels with hooked talons,

loci.virgil: vestigat lustrans, solum in certamina poscit.
comprensamque tenet pedibusque eviscerat uncis;

lines.diplomatic: Regnorum immemores turpiq; cupidine captos
lines.en: [those] forgetful of [their] kingdoms, and caught by base desire,

loci.virgil: regnorum immemores turpique cupidine captos.

lines.diplomatic: Maius adorta nefas maiõremq; orsa furorem
lines.en: having ventured a greater crime, and begun a greater madness,

loci.virgil: maius adorta nefas maioremque orsa furorem

lines.diplomatic: Mœnibus in patrijs regali splendida luxu
lines.en: within [her] native walls, splendid with royal luxury,

loci.virgil: moenibus in patriis atque inter tuta domorum
At domus interior regali splendida luxu

lines.diplomatic: Inter sacra deum iuuenes ante ora parentum
lines.en: amid the sacred rites of the gods, [and] youths before the faces of [their] parents,

loci.virgil: inter sacra deum nocturnique orgia Bacchi
impositique rogis iuvenes ante ora parentum:

lines.diplomatic: Per uarios sternit casus, muliebribus armis
lines.en: she lays low through various mischances — with womanly weapons

loci.virgil: per varios sternit casus. Accurrit Halaesus
Advenit qui vestra dies muliebribus armis

lines.diplomatic: Obuia multa uirum demittit corpora morti
lines.en: she sends down to death many bodies of men in her path,

loci.virgil: obvia multa virum demittit corpora morti:

lines.en: rolling [her] bloody gaze, she roars with bloody mouth,

loci.virgil: sanguineam torquens aciem, torvumque repente
inpavidus frangit telum et fremit ore cruento:

lines.diplomatic: Rumoresq́; serit uarios, cui tristia bella
lines.en: she sows various rumors — she for whom sad wars

loci.virgil: rumoresque serit varios ac talia fatur:
infernisque ciet tenebris, cui tristia bella

lines.diplomatic: Iræq́; insidiæq́;, & crimina noxia cordi
lines.en: and wraths, and treacheries, and harmful crimes are dear to [her] heart,

lines.diplomatic: Nate patris summi grates persoluere dignas
lines.en: O son of the highest father, to pay worthy thanks

loci.virgil: nate, patris summi qui tela Typhoia temnis,
urbe, domo, socias, grates persolvere dignas

lines.en: it is not within our power to have escaped [this] wicked race;

loci.virgil: addixi: satis est gentem effugisse nefandam.

lines.diplomatic: Quod superest, oro propius tua numina firmes
lines.en: for what remains, I pray, make firm your divine will more closely [upon us],

loci.virgil: Quod superest, oro, liceat dare tuta per undas
Adsis o tantum et propius tua numina firmes."

lines.diplomatic: Illa dolos dirumq́; nefas in pectore uersat
lines.en: she turns over in her heart tricks and dire wickedness,

loci.virgil: Illa dolos dirumque nefas in pectore versat,

lines.diplomatic: Eripe me his inuicte malis, uia prima salutis
lines.en: Snatch me, unconquered one, from these evils — the first way of safety [is this]:

loci.virgil: eripe me his, invicte, malis: aut tu mihi terram
qua tua te Fortuna sinet. Via prima salutis,

lines.diplomatic: Ad te confugio, pacem te poscimus omnes
lines.en: to you I flee for refuge; we all beg you for peace,

loci.virgil: ad te confugio et supplex tua numina posco.
Nulla salus bello: pacem te poscimus omnes,

lines.diplomatic: Vna omnes iuuenum primi prisciq́; Quirites
lines.en: together, all the foremost of the youth, and the ancient Quirites,

loci.virgil: una omnes iuvenum primi pauperque senatus
Una ingens Amiterna cohors priscique Quirites,

lines.diplomatic: Aspice nos, dira bellum cum gente gerendum
lines.en: look upon us — a war must be waged with a dread race,

loci.virgil: aspice nos; hoc tantum, et, si pietate meremur,
edico, et dira bellum cum gente gerendum.

lines.diplomatic: Tristius haud illis monstrum, mihi frigidus horror
lines.en: no grimmer monster than they — a cold horror [comes over] me,

loci.virgil: Tristius haud illis monstrum, nec saevior ulla
et terram tabo maculant.  Mihi frigidus horror

lines.diplomatic: Membra quatit, sonitumq́; pedum uocemq́; tremisco
lines.en: it shakes my limbs, and I tremble at the sound of feet and voice,

loci.virgil: prospicio, sonitumque pedum vocemque tremesco.

lines.diplomatic: Carpit enim uires paulatim, uritq́; uidendo
lines.en: for she saps [my] strength little by little, and burns [me] by the sight [of her],

loci.virgil: Carpit enim viris paulatim uritque videndo

lines.diplomatic: FOEMINA, dij talem terris auertite pestem.
lines.en: WOMAN — gods, avert such a plague from the earth!

loci.virgil: sidera---Di, talem terris avertite pestem!---

lines.diplomatic: NYMPHÆ, noster amor, paulo maiora canamus
lines.en: Nymphs, our love, let us sing of things a little greater.

loci.virgil: Nymphae, noster amor, Libethrides, aut mihi carmen,
Sicelides Musae, paulo maiora canamus!

lines.diplomatic: Arma inter Regum, Magno turbante tumultu
lines.en: Amid the arms of kings, with a great tumult raging,

loci.virgil: arma inter regum falsa formidine ludit.
Hic rem Romanam, magno turbante tumultu,

lines.diplomatic: Pastor Aristeus folijs ornatus oliuæ,
lines.en: The shepherd Aristeus, adorned with leaves of the olive,

loci.virgil: Pastor Aristaeus fugiens Peneia Tempe,
Ipse caput tonsae foliis ornatus olivae

lines.diplomatic: Fatidicæ Mantus, & Thusci filius amnis
lines.en: [Son] of fatidic Manto, and son of the Tuscan river,

loci.virgil: fatidicae Mantus et Tusci filius amnis,

lines.diplomatic: Carminibus patrijs Tyberini ad fluminis undam
lines.en: With ancestral songs, at the wave of the Tiberine river,

loci.virgil: carminibus patriis lancesque et liba feremus
Interea genitor Tiberini ad fluminis undam

lines.diplomatic: Suspiciens cælum lachrymis ita fatur abortis.

loci.virgil: suspiciens caelum tenditque ad sidera dextram:

lines.en: Alas, why have such great clouds girded the sky?

loci.virgil: "Heu! quianam tanti cinxerunt aethera nimbi?

lines.en: The heavens have thundered, and the winds, as if drawn up in column,

impulit in latus: ac venti, velut agmine facto,

Diripuere aras, it toto turbida caelo

lines.en: a storm of weapons, and an iron rain rushes on.

lines.en: Burning shields, and gleaming bronze, I see.

loci.virgil: Ardentis clipeos atque aera micantia cerno!"---

lines.diplomatic: Armorum sonitum toto Germania cælo
lines.en: The din of arms, through all the sky, Germania

loci.virgil: Armorum sonitum toto Germania caelo

lines.diplomatic: Audijt, & rauco strepuerunt cornua cantu:
lines.en: heard, and horns resounded with a hoarse blare;

loci.virgil: extulit et rauco strepuerunt cornua cantu,

lines.en: and trembling mothers pressed their children to their breasts.

loci.virgil: et trepidae matres pressere ad pectora natos.

lines.diplomatic: Stant belli causæ. en iterum crudelia retro
lines.en: The causes of war stand fixed. Behold, again the cruel fates, backward—

loci.virgil: stant belli causae, pugnatur comminus armis,

lines.en: A youth outstanding in beauty, seeking a new kingdom,

loci.virgil: abstulit atra dies et funere mersit acerbo;

loci.virgil: Balatu pecorum et crebris mugitibus amnes

lines.en: for you the clear lakes wept; near to Cremona,

Mantua, vae miserae nimium vicina Cremonae—

lines.en: beside the water, where the great [river] wanders with slow windings —

loci.virgil: propter aquam. Tardis ingens ubi flexibus errat

lines.en: behold, the nymphs bring in baskets, solaces for grief,

loci.virgil: intersintque patris lacrimis, solacia luctus

lines.en: small, for [a grief] so vast, yet owed to a wretched father;

loci.virgil: tu decus omne tuis. Postquam te fata tulerunt,

lines.en: discord arose among the kings with great commotion;

lines.en: wields thunderbolts; his proud emblem of war [is]

arduus agmen agens; cui, belli insigne superbum,

loci.virgil: asper, acerba tuens, retro redit, et neque terga

insula inexhaustis Chalybum generosa metallis.

lines.en: and the Morini, farthest of men, and the two-horned Rhine,

loci.virgil: extremique hominum Morini, Rhenusque bicornis,
