lines.en: and the turbid Ister, rolling its yellow sands —

loci.virgil: turbidus et torquens flaventis Hister harenas,

lines.en: but on the other side [he] snatches up a strong spear by force,

spes Italas; recalent nostro Thybrina fluenta

lines.diplomatic: Prolatio obtestor, pro maiestate tuorum
lines.en: for Latium I entreat, for the majesty of your kin —

loci.virgil: pro Latio obtestor, pro maiestate tuorum:

lines.diplomatic: Proijce tela manu. paribus se legibus ambæ
lines.en: cast the weapons from your hand. Let both [peoples], under equal laws,

loci.virgil: proice tela manu, sanguis meus!---

lines.diplomatic: Inuictæ gentes æterna in fœdera mittant
lines.en: unconquered nations, enter into an everlasting treaty.

loci.virgil: invictae gentes aeterna in foedera mittant.

lines.diplomatic: Nunc ad te, & tua, magne pater consulta reuertor
lines.en: Now I return to you, great father, and to your counsels;

loci.virgil: Nunc ad te et tua magna, pater, consulta revertor.

lines.diplomatic: Ad te confugio, & supplex, Rex optime Regum
lines.en: to you I flee for refuge, and, a suppliant, [to you,] best King of kings —

loci.virgil: ad te confugio et supplex tua numina posco.
Et responsa simul quae sint, rex optime, regis

lines.diplomatic: Quid grauidam bellis urbem, & corda aspera tentas
lines.en: why do you try the city big with wars, and hearts made harsh,

loci.virgil: quid gravidam bellis urbem et corda aspera temptas?

lines.diplomatic: Littus ad Ausonium [?] potuit quæ plurima uirtus
lines.en: to the Ausonian shore [?] — what very great valor could

loci.virgil: litus ad Ausonium tot per vada caerula vexit?
Nec quemquam incuso: potuit quae plurima virtus

lines.diplomatic: Esse, fuit; toto certatum est corpore Regni
lines.en: have been, it was; the whole body of the Realm contended.

lines.diplomatic: Desine iam tandem, precibusq; inflectere nostris
lines.en: Cease now at last, and be bent by our prayers,

loci.virgil: Desine iam tandem precibusque inflectere nostris,

lines.diplomatic: Cede Deo, nec te ullius uiolentia uincat,
lines.en: yield to god, and let no man's violence overcome you,

loci.virgil: Cede deo." Dixitque et proelia voce diremit.
adicias nec te ullius violentia vincat,

lines.diplomatic: Quin gnatam egregio genero(præq; omnibns unum
lines.en: rather, [give] your daughter to an outstanding son-in-law — and this one thing, before all others,

loci.virgil: unum illud tibi, nate dea, proque omnibus unum

lines.diplomatic: Prædicam, & repetens iterumq; iterumq, monebo)
lines.en: I shall proclaim, and repeating it again and again I shall urge —

lines.diplomatic: Des pater, & pacem hanc æterno fœdere iungas
lines.en: grant [this], father, and join this peace with an everlasting treaty.

loci.virgil: des, pater, et pacem hanc aeterno foedere iungas.

lines.diplomatic: Quo ferrum, quid ue hæc gentis tela irrita dextris?
lines.en: To what end the sword, or why these weapons, useless in the hands of this people?

loci.virgil: Quo ferrum quidve haec gerimus tela inrita dextris?

lines.diplomatic: Quod si tantus amor menti, si tanta cupido
lines.en: But if such great love is in your mind, if such great desire,

loci.virgil: Quod si tantus amor menti, si tanta cupido est,

lines.diplomatic: Arua aliena iugo premere, atque auertere prædas;
lines.en: to press foreign fields under the yoke, and carry off plunder,

loci.virgil: arva aliena iugo premere atque avertere praedas?

lines.diplomatic: Arma parate animis, nec longe scilicet hostes
lines.en: prepare your arms in spirit — for indeed the enemy is not far

loci.virgil: Arma parate animis et spe praesumite bellum,
experiare licet; nec longe scilicet hostes

lines.diplomatic: Quærendi uobis. Certatur limine in ipso
lines.en: for you to seek. The fight is joined on the very threshold

loci.virgil: nunc hi, nunc illi; certatur limine in ipso

lines.diplomatic: Ausoniæ, quæ tanta animis ignauia uenit?
lines.en: of Ausonia — what such great cowardice has come into your minds?

loci.virgil: Tyrrheni, quae tanta animis ignavia venit?

lines.diplomatic: Ecce inimicus atrox; cæsis insignis Achiuis
lines.en: Behold the fierce enemy, distinguished by the slaughtered Achaeans,

loci.virgil: ecce inimicus, atrox, magno stridore per auras
victor aget currum, caesis insignis Achivis.

lines.diplomatic: Victor ab Auroræ populis: summasq; minatur
lines.en: victor from the peoples of the Dawn: and he threatens the highest [citadels],

loci.virgil: victor ab Aurorae populis et litore rubro,
Fulminat Aeneas armis summasque minatur

lines.diplomatic: Deiecturum arces Italum, excidioq; daturum
lines.en: [threatening] to cast down the citadels of the Italians, and give [them] to ruin —

lines.diplomatic: Horresco referens, sedeantq; spectentq; Latini
lines.en: I shudder in relating it — and let the Latins sit and watch:

loci.virgil: horresco referens---immensis orbibus angues
desertorem Asiae (sedeant spectentque Latini),

lines.diplomatic: Regnatorem Asiæ spolijs Orientis onustum
lines.en: the ruler of Asia, laden with the spoils of the East,

loci.virgil: regnatorem Asiae.  Iacet ingens litore truncus,
Hunc tu olim caelo, spoliis Orientis onustum,

lines.diplomatic: Immanem ueluti pecora inter inertia tigrim
lines.en: like a monstrous tiger among sluggish cattle —

loci.virgil: immanem veluti pecora inter inertia tigrim

lines.diplomatic: Diuersa exilia, & diuersas quærere terras
lines.en: to seek scattered places of exile, and sundry lands

loci.virgil: diversa exsilia et desertas quaerere terras

lines.diplomatic: Cogemur, qui nunc lenti consedimus aruis
lines.en: we shall be forced, we who now sit idle on our fields.

loci.virgil: cogemur, qui nunc lenti consedimus arvis."

lines.diplomatic: Illi armis in regna ruunt. Crudelis ubique
lines.en: They rush with arms into the kingdoms. Cruel everywhere

loci.virgil: illi armis in regna ruunt." Nec plura locutus

lines.diplomatic: Luctus, ubique pauor, incuruant uiribus arcus
lines.en: the grief, everywhere the dread; they bend their bows with strength,

loci.virgil: Tum validis flexos incurvant viribus arcus

lines.diplomatic: Exhortantur equos; fundunt simul undique tela
lines.en: they spur on their horses; at once, from every side, they pour forth weapons,

loci.virgil: exhortantur equos; fundunt simul undique tela

lines.diplomatic: Crebra niuis ritu, cincti fulgentibus armis
lines.en: thick as snow, girded with shining arms,

loci.virgil: Ter circum accensos cincti fulgentibus armis

lines.diplomatic: Connixi incurrunt hastis; pars maxima glandes
lines.en: straining, they charge with spears; the greater part [hurl] leaden

loci.virgil: conixi incurrunt hastis primique ruina
nec clipei currusve sonant: pars maxima glandes

lines.diplomatic: Liuentis plumbi spargit: loca sulphure fumant
lines.en: bullets, livid, scattering [them]: the ground smokes with sulphur,

loci.virgil: dat lucem, et late circum loca sulphure fumant.

lines.diplomatic: AERE cauo, & subito cælum tonat omne fragore,
lines.en: with hollow bronze, and suddenly the whole sky thunders with a crash,

loci.virgil: aere cavo.  Invadunt socii, et nova proelia temptant,
procubuit subito et caelum tonat omne fragore.

lines.diplomatic: Nec longum in medio tempus, cum clamor ad aures
lines.en: and no long interval passes, when a clamor to the ears

loci.virgil: Nec longum in medio tempus, cum clamor ad auris

lines.diplomatic: Bellantum iuuenum, & duro sub Marte cadentum
lines.en: of warring young men, and of those falling beneath harsh Mars —

loci.virgil: bellantum iuvenum et duro sub Marte cadentum.

lines.diplomatic: Diuerso interea miscentur mœnia luctu;
lines.en: meanwhile the city walls are thrown into confusion with varied grief;

loci.virgil: Diverso interea miscentur moenia luctu,

lines.diplomatic: Iamq; sacerdotes magnam Mauortis ad urbem
lines.en: and now the priests, to the great city of Mars,

loci.virgil: iamque sacerdotes primusque Potitius ibant,
mittitur et magni Venulus Diomedis ad urbem,

lines.diplomatic: Velati lino uolitant, lustrantq; choreis
lines.en: clothed in linen, hasten, and encircle it with dances,

loci.virgil: Agnoscunt longe regem lustrantque choreis,

lines.diplomatic: Atria dependent lychni laquearibus aureis
lines.en: the halls; lamps hang from the gilded ceiling-panels.

loci.virgil: atria; dependent lychni laquearibus aureis

lines.diplomatic: Implorantq; Deos incensa altaria circum
lines.en: and they implore the gods, around the kindled altars;

loci.virgil: implorantque deos obtestanturque Latinum.
tum Salii ad cantus incensa altaria circum

lines.diplomatic: Haud mora festinant flentes, ostroq; decori
lines.en: without delay, weeping, they hasten, and, adorned with purple,

loci.virgil: haud mora, festinant flentes, aramque sepulchri
ductores auro volitant ostroque decori,

lines.diplomatic: Flent mœsti, mussantq; patres, pauperq; SENATVS
lines.en: the sorrowful fathers weep and murmur, and the poor SENATE —

loci.virgil: flent maesti mussantque patres. Hic undique clamor
una omnes iuvenum primi pauperque senatus

lines.diplomatic: Ipse gubernator, rerum cui summa potestas,
lines.en: the helmsman himself, to whom belongs the highest power over affairs,

loci.virgil: Ipse gubernator puppi Palinurus ab alta:
Tum pater omnipotens, rerum cui prima potestas,

lines.diplomatic: Dum paci medium se offert iustissimus unus
lines.en: while, most just, he alone offers himself as mediator for peace,

loci.virgil: dum paci medium se offert, iustissimus unus

lines.diplomatic: Cuncta uidens magno curarum fluctuat æstu
lines.en: seeing all things, is tossed on the great tide of cares;

loci.virgil: cuncta videns magno curarum fluctuat aestu,

lines.diplomatic: Exorat pacem Diuùm, uittasq́; resoluit
lines.en: he entreats the peace of the gods, and loosens the fillets

loci.virgil: exorat pacem divom, vittasque resolvit

lines.diplomatic: Sacrati capitis tendens ad sydera palmas
lines.en: of his consecrated head, stretching his palms to the stars,

loci.virgil: velum adversa ferit, fluctusque ad sidera tollit.

lines.diplomatic: Nequid inexpertum, Tyrio conspectus in ostro
lines.en: lest anything be left untried — conspicuous in Tyrian purple,

loci.virgil: illi victor ego et Tyrio conspectus in ostro

lines.diplomatic: Ora puer prima signans intonsa iuuenta
lines.en: a boy, marking his unshorn cheeks with the first [down of] youth,

loci.virgil: ora puer prima signans intonsa iuventa.

lines.diplomatic: Nomen aui referens, Augusta ad mœnia Regis
lines.en: bearing his grandfather's name, to the august walls of the King,

loci.virgil: nomen avi referens Priamus,---tua clara, Polite,
centum oratores augusta ad moenia regis

lines.diplomatic: Itq;, reditq; uiam toties, lachrymansq́;, gemensq́;
lines.en: goes and returns along the way so many times, weeping and groaning,

loci.virgil: itque reditque viam totiens. Quid Thesea, magnum
procubuit super atque haeret lacrimansque gemensque,

lines.diplomatic: Paciferæq́; manu ramum prætendit oliuæ,
lines.en: and holds out in his hand a branch of peace-bearing olive,

loci.virgil: paciferaeque manu ramum praetendit olivae:

lines.diplomatic: Ante annos animumq; gerens, curamq; uirilem.
lines.en: bearing, beyond his years, a mind and a manly care.

loci.virgil: ante annos animumque gerens curamque virilem,

lines.diplomatic: Ipse sedens clauumq; regit, uelisq́; ministrat
lines.en: He himself, sitting, guides the rudder, and tends the sails,

loci.virgil: ipse sedens clavumque regit velisque ministrat.

lines.diplomatic: Iam senior, sed cruda Deo, uiridisq́; senectus.
lines.en: now older, but his old age tough as a god's, and green with strength.

loci.virgil: iam senior, sed cruda deo viridisque senectus.

lines.diplomatic: Ergo concilium magnum, primosq́; suorum
lines.en: Therefore a great council, and the foremost of his own,

loci.virgil: Ergo concilium magnum primosque suorum

lines.diplomatic: Imperio, accitos Athesim nunc propter amœnum
lines.en: summoned by [his] command, now beside pleasant Athesis [the Adige],

loci.virgil: sive Padi ripis Athesim seu propter amoenum,

lines.diplomatic: Ire iubet, quorum melior sententia menti
lines.en: he orders to go — [those] whose judgment in mind is better —

loci.virgil: At Capys, et quorum melior sententia menti,
At Capys, et quorum melior sententia menti,

lines.diplomatic: Iura dabunt, legesq́; uiris, ritusq́; sacrorum.
lines.en: shall give laws, and statutes to the men, and the rites of the sacred things.

lines.diplomatic: O páter, o hominum, diuumq; æterna potestas
lines.en: O father, O eternal power over men and gods,

loci.virgil: "O pater, O hominum rerumque aeterna potestas!

lines.diplomatic: Spero equidem, si quid pietas antiqua labores
lines.en: I hope indeed, if ancient piety at all [regards] the toils

loci.virgil: Spero equidem mediis, si quid pia numina possunt,
Troianos, si quid pietas antiqua labores

lines.diplomatic: Respicit humanos, crimenq́;, caputq́; malorum
lines.en: [if it] regards human [affairs], that the crime and the head of these evils

loci.virgil: se causam clamat crimenque caputque malorum,

lines.diplomatic: Supplicia hausurum, laniatum corpore toto
lines.en: will drain punishments, torn in his whole body,

loci.virgil: supplicia hausurum scopulis, et nomine Dido
Atque hic Priamiden laniatum corpore toto

lines.diplomatic: Romanoq; foro flamma crepitante cremari
lines.en: and in the Roman forum to be burned with crackling flame —

loci.virgil: Romanoque foro et lautis mugire Carinis.
[atque omnem ornatum flamma crepitante cremari]

lines.diplomatic: Cernere erit; tantas audetis tollere moles
lines.en: it will be given to see. Do you dare to raise such vast turmoil,

loci.virgil: miscere, et tantas audetis tollere moles?
miscere, et tantas audetis tollere moles?

lines.diplomatic: Gens effrena uirum septem subiecta trioni?
lines.en: an unbridled race of men, subject to the seven [stars] of the north?

loci.virgil: gens effrena virum Rhiphaeo tunditur euro
Talis Hyperboreo septem subiecta trioni

lines.diplomatic: Tanta ne uos generis tenuit fiducia uestri?
lines.en: Has such great confidence in your lineage possessed you?

loci.virgil: "Tantane vos generis tenuit fiducia vestri?

lines.diplomatic: At sperate Deos memores fandi, atque nefandi.
lines.en: But hope that the gods are mindful of right and wrong.

loci.virgil: at sperate deos memores fandi atque nefandi.

lines.diplomatic: Ipsi has sacrilego pendetis sanguine pœnas.
lines.en: You yourselves shall pay these penalties with sacrilegious blood.

loci.virgil: "Tu tamen interea calido mihi sanguine poenas

lines.diplomatic: Discite iustitam moniti, & non temnere diuos.
lines.en: Learn justice, being warned, and not to scorn the gods.

loci.virgil: "Discite iustitiam moniti, et non temnere divos."

lines.diplomatic: Nate patris summi, tuq; o sanctissima vates
lines.en: Son of the highest father, and you, O most holy prophetess,

loci.virgil: nate, patris summi qui tela Typhoia temnis,
gloria Dardaniae. Tuque, O sanctissima vates,

lines.diplomatic: Quæ Thuscum Tyberim, & Romana palatia seruas
lines.en: who guard the Tuscan Tiber, and the Roman palaces —

loci.virgil: quae Tuscum Tiberim et Romana Palatia servas,

lines.diplomatic: Diua parens, præsens nostro succurre labori
lines.en: divine mother, be present, and succor our labor;

loci.virgil: diva parens." Sic effatus vestigia pressit,
"Tu, dea, tu praesens nostro succurre labori,

lines.diplomatic: Romanosq; tuos iactatos æquore toto
lines.en: and your Romans, tossed upon the whole sea,

loci.virgil: His accensa super, iactatos aequore toto

lines.diplomatic: Dij maris, & terræ, tempestatumq; potentes
lines.en: gods of the sea and of the land, and powerful over the storms,

loci.virgil: "Di maris et terrae tempestatumque potentes,

lines.diplomatic: Hos inter motus tantis surgentibus undis
lines.en: amid these disturbances, with such great waves rising,

loci.virgil: Hos inter motus, medio in flagrante tumultu,
deficeret tantis navis surgentibus undis.

lines.diplomatic: Ferte uiam uento facilem, & spirate secundi,
lines.en: grant an easy path to the wind, and blow favorably,

loci.virgil: ferte viam vento facilem et spirate secundi."

lines.diplomatic: Et placidi seruate pios, gentemq; togatam
lines.en: and, being calm, preserve the pious, and the toga-clad race —

loci.virgil: et placidi servate pios!" Tum litore funem
Romanos rerum dominos gentemque togatam:

lines.diplomatic: Sit Latium , sint Albani per secula Reges
lines.en: let there be Latium, let there be Alban kings through the ages,

loci.virgil: Sit Latium, sint Albani per saecula reges,

lines.diplomatic: Hac casti maneant in relligione nepotes
lines.en: let their chaste descendants abide in this observance,

loci.virgil: hac casti maneant in religione nepotes.

lines.diplomatic: Et nati natorum, & qui nascentur ab illis.
lines.en: and children's children, and those who shall be born from them.

loci.virgil: et nati natorum, et qui nascentur ab illis."

lines.diplomatic: At tu magne pater , puraq; in ueste sacerdos
lines.en: But you, great father, and the priest in pure vesture,

loci.virgil: aut tu, magne pater divom, miserere tuoque
procedunt castris, puraque in veste sacerdos

lines.diplomatic: Tuq; o Tybri tuo genitor cum flumine sancto
lines.en: and you, O father Tiber, with your holy stream —

loci.virgil: tuque, o Thybri tuo genitor cum flumine sancto,

lines.diplomatic: Durate, & uosmet rebus seruate secundis
lines.en: endure, and preserve yourselves for kinder circumstances.

loci.virgil: Durate, et vosmet rebus servate secundis."

lines.diplomatic: O passi grauiora, dabit Deus his quoque finem.
lines.en: O you who have suffered heavier things, God will give an end to these too.

loci.virgil: O passi graviora, dabit deus his quoque finem.

lines.diplomatic: In freta dum fluuij current, uulgata per orbem
lines.en: As long as rivers run to the sea — spread through the world —

loci.virgil: In freta dum fluvii current, dum montibus umbrae
bellaque iam fama totum volgata per orbem,

lines.diplomatic: Intemerata fides, Capitoli immobile saxum
lines.en: inviolate faith shall inhabit the immovable rock of the Capitol,

loci.virgil: intemerata fides, oro, miserere laborum
dum domus Aeneae Capitoli immobile saxum

lines.diplomatic: Accolet, imperiumq, pater Romanus habebit,
lines.en: shall dwell beside [it], and the Roman father shall hold empire,

lines.diplomatic: Missus in imperium , cæli cui sydera parent,
lines.en: sent into command, to whom the stars of heaven are obedient,

loci.virgil: missus in imperium magnum. Cui deinde subibit,
cui pecudum fibrae, caeli cui sidera parent

lines.diplomatic: Inferniq; lacus , atque altæ mœnia Romæ
lines.en: and the infernal lakes, and the walls of lofty Rome.

loci.virgil: infernique lacus, Aeaeaeque insula Circae,
Albanique patres, atque altae moenia Romae.

lines.diplomatic: Ille canit : placidi strauerunt æquora uenti
lines.en: He sings: the calm winds have smoothed the seas,

loci.virgil: ille canit: pulsae referunt ad sidera valles;
factus honos: placidi straverunt aequora venti,

lines.diplomatic: Intonuit læuum, & uibratus ab æthere fulgor
lines.en: it thundered on the left [in a good omen], and a flash quivering from the sky

loci.virgil: intonuit laevum, et de caelo lapsa per umbras
Namque inproviso vibratus ab aethere fulgor

lines.diplomatic: Collectasq; fugat nubes, solemq; reducit.
lines.en: puts to flight the gathered clouds, and brings back the sun.

loci.virgil: collectasque fugat nubes, solemque reducit.

lines.diplomatic: Sole recens orto, magnam Mauortis ad urbem
lines.en: The sun having newly risen, near the great city of Mars,

loci.virgil: sole recens orto aut noctem ducentibus astris.
mittitur et magni Venulus Diomedis ad urbem,

lines.diplomatic: Incumbens tereti DAMON sic cæpit oliuæ.
lines.en: Leaning upon a smooth olive-staff, DAMON thus began:

loci.virgil: incumbens tereti Damon sic coepit olivae.

lines.diplomatic: Aggredere ò magnos (aderit iam tempus) honores
lines.en: Undertake, O, great honors — the time will soon be at hand —

loci.virgil: Adgredere o magnos—aderit iam tempus—honores,

lines.diplomatic: Cara Deùm soboles, magnæ spes altera Romæ
lines.en: dear offspring of the gods, second hope of great Rome,

loci.virgil: et iuxta Ascanius, magnae spes altera Romae,

lines.diplomatic: Macte noua uirtute puer, diuine poeta,
lines.en: all hail to you for your fresh valor, boy, divine poet:

loci.virgil: "Macte nova virtute, puer: sic itur ad astra,
Tale tuum carmen nobis, divine poeta,

lines.diplomatic: Quid struis? aut qua spe tu nunc in montibus erras
lines.en: What are you devising? Or with what hope do you now wander in the mountains,

loci.virgil: quid struis, aut qua spe Libycis teris otia terris?
ah, virgo infelix, tu nunc in montibus erras:

lines.diplomatic: Threicia fretus cithara, fidibusq; canoris?
lines.en: relying on the Thracian lyre and tuneful strings?

loci.virgil: Threcia fretus cithara fidibusque canoris,

lines.diplomatic: Desine iam tandem Tyrio conspectus in ostro
lines.en: Cease now at last, conspicuous in Tyrian purple,

loci.virgil: Desine iam tandem precibusque inflectere nostris,
illi victor ego et Tyrio conspectus in ostro

lines.diplomatic: Atque humiles habitare casas, & figere ceruos
lines.en: and to dwell in lowly cottages, and to shoot deer;

loci.virgil: atque humilis habitare casas, et figere cervos,

lines.diplomatic: Vtere sorte tua; nemorum Latonia custos
lines.en: enjoy your [own] lot; let the Latonian guardian of the groves

loci.virgil: "utere sorte tua. Miseri te siqua parentis
astrorum decus et nemorum Latonia custos

lines.diplomatic: Riparumq́; toros, & depressas conualleis
lines.en: herself inhabit the grassy river-banks, and the sunken valleys,

loci.virgil: riparumque toros et prata recentia rivis

lines.diplomatic: Ipsa colat, fatis huc te poscentibus affer,
lines.en: and bring yourself hither, since the fates now demand you —

loci.virgil: ipsa colat; nobis placeant ante omnia silvae.
ostentat: fatis huc te poscentibus adfers.

lines.diplomatic: Maior agit Deus, atque opera ad maiora remittit
lines.en: a greater god drives [you], and sends [you] back to greater works,

loci.virgil: maior agit deus atque opera ad maiora remittit."

lines.diplomatic: Muleentem tigres, & agentem carmine quercus
lines.en: [you] who soothe tigers, and move oaks with your song.

loci.virgil: mulcentem tigres et agentem carmine quercus;

lines.diplomatic: Europæ atque Asiæ præstat componere fluctus;
lines.en: it is better to still the waves of Europe and of Asia;

loci.virgil: Europae atque Asiae fatis concurrerit orbis,
Quos ego---sed motos praestat componere fluctus.

lines.diplomatic: Hoc uirtutis opus, fratrem ne desere frater
lines.en: this is virtue's task: do not, brother, forsake your brother.

loci.virgil: hoc virtutis opus. Troiae sub moenibus altis
dicta dabas. Morere et fratrem ne desere frater."
